title: extend service knowledge capabilities for docs like the infra telemetry wiring. must be done correctly and made sure no staleness risk
release-flow: dev integrates, main = stable release line (clone-safe for non-technical users)
description:
## PROBLEM

Three active repos under `~/dev/` — `specialists`, `xtmux`, `core` — currently merge all sprint work directly to `main` under PR protection. Non-technical users who clone `main` mid-sprint receive a half-done product: the branch tip tracks every dev merge, so a clone during a 20-PR sprint lands on an incoherent, non-shippable state.

Root cause: `main` is both integration target AND release line. No branch stays frozen between releases.

## SCOPE (agreed model)

Applies to all three repos: `~/dev/specialists`, `~/dev/xtmux`, `~/dev/core` (shorthand: `~/dev/{specialists,xtmux,core}`).

- `dev` = integration branch. All sprint PRs land here. Allowed to be half-done mid-sprint. Contributors target `dev`.
- `main` = release line, stays default branch (bare `git clone` hits stable code). Advances ONLY at release boundaries, not per dev merge. A release = "sprint done, verified" → merge `dev -> main` → tag `vX.Y.Z`.
- Non-technical users clone `main` → always get a coherent, shippable product. Half-done state lives on `dev` and never reaches `main`.
- Key rule: `dev -> main` = release. `main` does not auto-track `dev`.

## HOTFIX POLICY (decided)

Mid-sprint `dev` is unstable, so `dev -> main` merge is not viable for shipping a fix.
- Hotfix = cherry-pick to `main` as patch release (`vX.Y.Z+1`), AND land the same fix on `dev` for next sprint release.
- Chosen over `hotfix/*` branch + back-merge (lazier, fewer branches).

## WORK ITEMS (rough — refine when promoted from draft)

- [ ] For each repo in `~/dev/{specialists,xtmux,core}`:
  - [ ] Branch protection on `dev`: PRs required, required CI status checks, linear history.
  - [ ] Tighten `main`: only `dev -> main` merge PRs accepted; keep default branch = main; required CI.
  - [ ] Add required status checks (CI: lint + test) on both branches if not present.
  - [ ] Write one-page CONTRIBUTING note: PRs target `dev`; releases cut from `dev -> main` merge + tag; hotfix = cherry-pick to `main` + land on `dev`.
- [ ] Define release cadence guardrail per repo: do not let `main` go stale (stale main = different complaint, same dissatisfaction).
- [ ] Decide per-repo CI workflow details (stacks may differ across the three repos).

## TBD

- Per-repo CI stack details (specialists / xtmux / core may differ).
- Whether all three adopt the model in the same pass or phased.
- Release cadence per repo (may differ).

## CONTEXT

Filed under specialists:xtmux territory. Work to be done at a later point. Created as draft contract (contract:draft label) until promoted to ready before dispatch.

title: Ack git-cliff rollout: tune scopes + reconcile CHANGELOG
description:
git-cliff was rolled out across all ~/dev and ~/projects repos in one batch (8fabb93). This bead is the ack + tuning gate for THIS repo.

## WHAT LANDED
- changelog/cliff.toml — GENERIC type-based parsers only (feat->Added, fix->Fixed,
  perf->Performance, docs|chore|build|ci|test|refactor|style->Project maintenance,
  everything else->Other changes). Version-bump commits are skipped.
- header = "" on purpose, so the CHANGELOG keeps its own title and --prepend never
  stacks a second header on top of it.
- Commit links point at this repo's own origin remote.
- CHANGELOG.md: generated fresh if absent; otherwise --prepend --unreleased only.
  Verified non-destructive — 0 existing lines lost in every repo that had one.

## WHY THIS BEAD IS P0
The config is deliberately generic and is NOT tuned to this repo. Until someone acks it:
- Real work may be landing under 'Other changes' instead of a meaningful section.
- Scope names used by this repo's commits have no parser entry.

## TO DO
1. Run: git-cliff --config changelog/cliff.toml --unreleased  (inspect, do not write)
2. Count entries falling into 'Other changes'. If more than a couple, add scope parsers
   ABOVE the generic ones, e.g. { message = "^feat\\(api\\)", group = "API" }.
3. Document the scope taxonomy in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md so the agents that write the
   commits actually follow it — the taxonomy is useless if only the parser knows it.
4. If this repo had a hand-written CHANGELOG, reconcile the generated format against
   the existing style (they will not match).
5. Regenerate with --prepend --unreleased. NEVER use -o / plain generate on a repo with
   a hand-written CHANGELOG — it rebuilds from the git log and drops every hand-written
   line (measured: 362 lines would be lost in specialists).

## DO NOT
- Do not run git-cliff without --prepend on a repo that already has a CHANGELOG.
- Nothing was pushed. Review the commit before pushing.
notes:
RESWEEPED — config now renders commit BODIES, not just subjects.

The first sweep only templated {{ commit.message }}, throwing away the rich bodies the
agents already write. cliff.toml now renders {% if commit.body %}, so a changelog entry
carries the full rationale, bead id, PR number, and file/env details straight from git.
Verified on market-data: generated entries now match the hand-written ones in substance.

All changelogs were restored to their exact pre-sweep state and re-prepended.
Measured: 0 pre-existing lines lost in every repo that already had a CHANGELOG.

## REMAINING TUNING (this bead)
1. SCOPES — parsers are still generic (type-based only). Run:
     git-cliff --config changelog/cliff.toml --unreleased
   Count entries under 'Other changes'. Add repo-specific scope parsers ABOVE the
   generic ones, e.g. { message = "^feat\\(api\\)", group = "API" }.
2. COMMIT BODIES ARE NOW THE CHANGELOG. Document that in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md: the
   body is what readers see, so agents should write it for a reader, not a reviewer.
   Squash-merge commits currently dump the raw PR bullet list verbatim — verbose.
3. FORMAT — repos with a hand-written CHANGELOG have two styles stacked. Reconcile.

## HARD RULE
NEVER run git-cliff without --prepend on a repo that has a hand-written CHANGELOG.
It rebuilds from the git log and drops every hand-written line (measured: 362 lines
would be lost in specialists). Always: --unreleased --prepend.

Nothing was pushed. Review before pushing.

No scope parsers added: large fallthrough is unconventional/auto-backup commits with no clean taxonomy. title: board-audit exporter: sanitize transport projection to close gitleaks generic-api-key recurrence
description:
## PROBLEM

Every `board-audit pr-checkpoint <PR>` and every `board-audit-export-wt checkpoint` currently produces gitleaks `generic-api-key` findings against the committed transport tree. The dominant hits (~40 on infra checkpoints) are on `.xtrm/board-audit/exports/export-<STAMP>/raw-beads.jsonl` on records of shape:

```
{"_type":"memory","key":"<high-entropy-slug>","value":"..."}
```

The field literally named `key` next to a high-entropy slug is exactly the pattern generic-api-key detects. A handful of additional hits occur on `work-packages/*.json` on bead description/notes prose.

This creates a recurring baseline-maintenance loop: every checkpoint would need `.gitleaksignore` fingerprint churn if we treated symptoms. That is a security-regression posture, not a fix.

## ROOT CAUSE

`bd export --all` emits Beads memory records with a field literally named `key`. Board-audit copies raw acquisition into the committed transport tree unchanged. The Beads/Dolt schema is authoritative and MUST NOT change. Only the transport projection changes.

## SCOPE

- `packages/board-audit/board-audit-core` — sanitize `raw-beads.jsonl` after acquisition, before commit.
- `packages/board-audit/tests/` — deterministic gitleaks harness (pinned v8.30.1, tmp git repos, 6 required results).
- `packages/board-audit/tests/` — PR-checkpoint recursion regression test.
- `packages/board-audit/README.md` — schema-version note.

## OUT OF SCOPE

- Beads/Dolt schema (unchanged).
- `.gitleaksignore` allowlist / wildcards / rule-weakening / entropy lowering / disabling generic-api-key.
- Automatic fingerprint append.
- Fresh Infra PR #362 board-audit checkpoint (coordinator handles after merge).

## DESIGN CHOICE (A)

Rename memory-record transport shape: `_type=memory` → `_type=memory-slug-v2`, `key` → `memory_slug`, add `_schema_version=2`. Value preserved verbatim. No board-audit code path consumes `_type=memory` records; verified via grep — only issue-type records feed derivation.

## CROSS-REPO EVIDENCE

Mercury infra bd tracks the cross-repo evidence bundle under `infra-tq2v` (discovered-from `infra-pq3f`). This xtrm bead is the code-owner counterpart. Do NOT mirror `infra-tq2v` in xtrm.

## ACCEPTANCE

- Deterministic harness under `packages/board-audit/tests/` PASS on 6 required results (A–F).
- Existing tests PASS.
- No `.gitleaksignore` added/modified.
- No wildcards / rule / entropy weakening.
- PR opened on xtrm main referencing infra-tq2v cross-repo evidence source.

title: security-auditor: harden XTS dangerous-command gate and history privacy
description:
## PROBLEM
The deterministic classifier allows trivial high-risk bypasses through absolute command paths, shell -c, env assignments, git global options, and xargs, while false-positive splitting quoted literals. Fresh shell-hook state can also be created with permissive modes and stores unredacted raw history.

## SUCCESS
The v1 gate conservatively detects the PRD high-risk families across common wrappers/path forms without parsing quoted literals as commands; recognized commands cannot execute without approval; shell-history state has private permissions and secret-bearing history is handled per explicit release policy.

## SCOPE
packages/xts/src/safety/**, src/history/hook.bash, hook.zsh, history/shell.mjs, related tests; pi-guardrails reference read-only.

## NON_GOALS
No policy editor, always/session allow, full shell AST, or full Guardrails dependency.

## CONSTRAINTS
Security boundary is deterministic and deny-safe. State exact supported grammar and residual bypass ceiling. Add adversarial tests first. SCRUTINY: high.

## VALIDATION
Test /bin/rm, sh/bash -c, env assignments, git -C destructive operations, xargs, quoted literals, deny no-exec sentinel, hook permissions, and secret persistence policy; run npm test and security review.

## OUTPUT
Threat cases, implementation/test evidence, residual bypasses, and operator-visible limitations.
close_reason: PASS after three review-fix loops and fresh independent verification. Classifier: 30-probe static set green (paths, wrappers/env, nested shells incl. env -S and ANSI-C, git options, xargs, find -exec, kill variants, rm -- operands, !/coproc/command -p/exec -a/setsid -f/stdbuf, control grammar) with position-aware scanning eliminating benign false positives; deny-before-exec preserved (runtime sentinel). Privacy: Bash/Zsh hooks redact generic/spaced secrets, password/bearer/RSA forms BEFORE persistence; live zsh -f -i probe: prior command captured, 0 secret leaks, hook stdout 0 bytes, modes dir 700 / files 600, no temp leftovers. Focused tests classify 21/21, shell 13/13; full suite 129/129 isolated. Residual documented ceiling: aliases/functions/indirection/obfuscation/full AST.

title: bridge/specialist-bridge use pi-ai/compat getModel — misses custom providers from ~/.pi/agent/models.json (e.g. commandcode)
description:
## Symptom

Real smoke against mercury/infra with SRE Specialist JSONs whose execution.model resolves to a Pi custom-provider ID (e.g. commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) fails at dispatch:

  dispatch threw: model not found: commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash

## Root cause

experiments/agentsession-sre-chain-vertical-slice/src/agents/bridge.ts:127-133 and src/agents/specialist-bridge.ts:94-101 both do:

  const primary = getModel(provider, id);  // from @earendil-works/pi-ai/compat

pi-ai/compat's getModel only resolves *built-in* providers (getBuiltinModel). Providers declared in ~/.pi/agent/models.json under `providers.<name>` (baseUrl + apiKey + api + authHeader + models[]) are custom — pi-coding-agent's own CLI loads them via core/model-runtime.js (class ModelRuntime), not via pi-ai/compat.

Built-in providers pi-ai/compat resolves in this env: anthropic, deepseek, google, nvidia, opencode-go, zai. Custom providers registered in ~/.pi/agent/models.json (this machine: commandcode, nano-gpt, nvidia, qwencloud, zai) are invisible to bridge.ts.

## Repro

  bun scripts/inspect-specialist.ts --repo <target> --name sre-coordinator
    -> resolves model string commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (compiler passes it through)
  bun src/cli/main.ts --repo <target> --specialist-json required --incident ...
    -> step.failed 'dispatch threw: model not found: commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash'
    -> reducer escalates chain

Test evidence: .chain-runs/sre-smoke-v2-20260819T010347Z/run-sre-85e55/forensics/events.jsonl

## Fix direction

bridge.ts + specialist-bridge.ts should route through ModelRuntime (or an equivalent adapter that unifies built-in + custom providers). Options:

1. Instantiate ModelRuntime from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, expose a wrapper getModelUnified(provider, id) that checks built-in first then custom via ModelRuntime.getAvailable(...).
2. Preflight: at bridge init, read ~/.pi/agent/models.json, and for each custom provider call pi-ai's registerProvider(...) (if exposed) with its baseUrl/api/apiKey/models.
3. Change Specialist JSON convention to only use built-in provider IDs (loses commandcode/nano-gpt/qwencloud gateway wrapping — arguably out of scope for the runtime to enforce).

Preferred: (1) — matches what Pi CLI does natively.

## Scope discipline

Same as xtrm-pq1.1: this is a runtime-integration defect, not a Specialist JSON cognition defect. Belongs to the next implementation workstream (PREPARE + capability resolver + activation supervisor), not this reconciliation campaign.
notes: Proven fix: src/agents/model-resolver.ts (NEW, 47 lines) — falls through pi-ai/compat built-ins to ~/.pi/agent/models.json catalog. commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash resolved end-to-end across all 6 chain steps today. Also required: src/chain/topology.ts DEFAULT_MODEL swapped to commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash starved reviewer in a prior run). Patches in worktree branch web/full-specialist-json-loader-2026-08-18. Handoff: experiments/agentsession-sre-chain-vertical-slice/handoff/2026-08-19-real-infra-smoke/patches/current-src/{model-resolver,topology}.ts.
close_reason: Fixed + verified. model-resolver.ts unifies built-in (pi-ai/compat) + custom providers (~/.pi/agent/models.json); smoke_bridge.ts dispatched coordinator-entry on commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, reached agent_end with evidence_publish(coordinator.decision)+channel_post(work.turn). Commit 16a4d52. See memory xtrm-pq1-2-verified-bridge-specialist-bridge-route.

title: Resolve planning output-contract contradiction (F2)
description:
# PROBLEM

Major. For intent planning, buildStructuredPrompt's output_format (src/prompt.mjs:136-140) tells the model "Return Markdown with exact headers: ## PROBLEM ..." with no sentinel, while BASE_RULES (src/prompt.mjs:36-43), appended to every request by buildSystemPrompt (:96-101), demands "Return exactly one <xtprompt>...</xtprompt> block and nothing outside it." completeRewrite requires the sentinel via isActionableRewrite. A model following the task-specific header instruction produces no sentinel, fails the first attempt, and is forced through a retry (extra cost and latency) or fails entirely. This affects every planning-shaped request (explicit --intent planning and auto-detected).

# SUCCESS

Planning requests carry a single, non-contradictory output contract. The first attempt succeeds for planning output in the common case. Either planning output is required inside the sentinel (recommended: "Return Markdown with the exact headers inside the <xtprompt> block"), or planning is exempted from the sentinel requirement and completeRewrite parses planning output directly. A regression test locks the chosen contract: the generated system prompt for a planning request contains no contradiction, and a valid planning-shaped response parses on the first attempt.

# SCOPE

src/prompt.mjs (buildStructuredPrompt output_format at :136-140, BASE_RULES at :36-43, buildSystemPrompt at :96-101; if parsing changes: parseSentinel/:180-185 and src/app.mjs completeRewrite/:350-381), test/prompt.test.mjs, test/app.test.mjs.

# NON_GOALS

- No change to the planning header set (## PROBLEM/## SUCCESS/## SCOPE/## NON_GOALS/## CONSTRAINTS/## VALIDATION/## OUTPUT) unless a decision records it.
- No change to other intents' contracts.

# CONSTRAINTS

- The chosen contract must be testable via the generated system prompt text (no model calls required).
- Keep the sentinel as the parse boundary for non-planning intents; if planning becomes sentinel-free, isolate that branch explicitly.
- README's planning usage examples must still work with the chosen contract.

# VALIDATION

- [ ] Test: buildPromptRequest with intent planning -> system prompt contains a single consistent output instruction (either sentinel-wrapped headers or an explicit sentinel-free contract).
- [ ] Test: a realistic planning-shaped model response (headers inside/without sentinel per the chosen contract) passes isActionableRewrite/parse on the first attempt.
- [ ] Existing planning contract-header test (prompt.test.mjs:68-86) stays green or is updated deliberately with the new contract.
- [ ] Full suite green.

# OUTPUT

Changed files, the chosen contract (sentinel-wrapped vs sentinel-free planning) with one-line rationale, test evidence, note on whether auto-detected planning requests also benefit (they use the same buildStructuredPrompt path).
close_reason: F2 fixed: planning output_format now requires exactly one <xtprompt> block containing the Markdown headers, matching BASE_RULES; no contradiction. Regression tests lock contract + first-attempt parse (no retry). 47 tests green.

title: Rework the vague-draft heuristic (F3)
description:
# PROBLEM

Major. isVagueDraft (src/prompt.mjs:47-54) classifies any prompt of 7 or fewer words as vague unless it contains a newline, colon, hash, digit, or dotted path. The README's own examples fail: `echo "analyze this failure" | xtprompt --intent analysis` exits 2 with "prompt is too vague" (empirically confirmed), and "implement a health command for the cli", "plan the migration", and "write a release checklist for this package" (exactly 7 words) all trigger the vague path. The concreteness checks (:50) run after the length gate (:49), so short concrete prompts like "fix bug 42" are always vague. This breaks documented usage in normal use: piped one-shots fail hard, TTY users get a surprise clarification question.

# SUCCESS

Short concrete prompts are not classified vague. The heuristic distinguishes underspecified drafts (bare "help", vague-word-only sentences) from concrete ones (action verb + named object) without requiring artificial length. README examples are verified against the new heuristic and either pass or are replaced with passing examples. The clarified-draft flow still triggers for genuinely vague input.

# SCOPE

src/prompt.mjs (isVagueDraft at :47-54, VAGUE_WORDS at :5-17), test/prompt.test.mjs (isVagueDraft tests at :22-29), README.md (usage examples), test/app.test.mjs (tests whose drafts rely on the old threshold: check the argv drafts in the harness and each test that expects exit 2 or clarification).

# NON_GOALS

- No change to the clarification UX (one question on TTY, exit 2 when piped, --no-clarify fail-fast).
- No change to buildClarifiedDraft.

# CONSTRAINTS

- Reorder so the structural concreteness checks (newline/colon/hash, digit, dotted path) run before any length-based gate, or fold them into one decision.
- The new heuristic must keep "help" and vague-word-only sentences vague.
- Update every test draft and README example affected by the threshold change; the suite must stay green.

# VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests for the new heuristic: "analyze this failure" false; "help" true; "help me improve this prompt today" true; "fix bug 42" false; "deploy to production" decision recorded (expected: false unless deliberate); 7-word concrete prompts false.
- [ ] README piped example verified end-to-end: `echo "analyze this failure" | node src/cli.mjs --intent analysis` no longer exits 2 before model setup (it may fail later on model/auth, but not on vagueness).
- [ ] Existing vague-flow tests (app.test.mjs:106-155) updated and green.
- [ ] Full suite green.

# OUTPUT

Changed files, the new decision table (input class -> vague yes/no), README diff, test evidence, note on any test drafts that needed updating and why.
close_reason: F3 fixed: structural concreteness checks now run before length gate; word-count gate replaced by all-vague-words check. 'analyze this failure', 'fix bug 42', README examples concrete; 'help' stays vague. README verified, no change needed. 48 tests green.

title: Fix auto-intent misclassification (F8)
description:
# PROBLEM

Major. INTENT_RULES (src/prompt.mjs:19-24) checks planning first, and the planning pattern set includes generic keywords constraints, validation, and plan. Development prompts routinely mention constraints and validation, so they auto-classify as planning (empirically confirmed: "Implement a standalone prompt CLI with explicit constraints, validation, and output behavior." -> planning; "Implement a release checklist for packages/xtprompt with validation." -> planning). Because planning forces the ## PROBLEM/## SCOPE header output contract, a development rewrite is silently converted into a planning-shaped prompt.

# SUCCESS

Auto-detection returns development (or the appropriate intent) for prompts whose primary action is implement/build/create/develop even when they mention constraints or validation. Planning is detected only on strong planning signals (## headers, plan/planning as the leading action, migration/rollout framing). Detection order and keyword sets are covered by regression tests.

# SCOPE

src/prompt.mjs (INTENT_RULES at :19-24), test/prompt.test.mjs (detectIntent tests at :14-20), test/app.test.mjs if any JSON-intent assertions depend on auto-detection.

# NON_GOALS

- No change to explicit --intent handling (it already bypasses detection).
- No change to the planning header output format itself (that is F2's scope).

# CONSTRAINTS

- Keyword changes must not flip genuinely planning-shaped prompts (e.g. "Plan this migration with ## SCOPE") away from planning.
- Keep the rule list exhaustive over INTENTS; detectIntent must still return one of the six documented intents.
- Reconcile with F2's contract outcome (planning output shape) so the two changes do not fight.

# VALIDATION

- [ ] Tests: development prompts containing "constraints" and "validation" -> development; "Plan this migration with ## SCOPE" -> planning; analysis/refactor/generic cases unchanged.
- [ ] The repo's own test drafts that currently auto-classify as planning are re-checked and the expected intent asserted.
- [ ] Full suite green.

# OUTPUT

Changed files, the new planning detection rule with rationale, the full intent decision table before/after, test evidence.
close_reason: F8 fixed: planning requires strong signals (## headers, non_goals, leading plan, 'plan the', migration/rollout plan framing); bare constraints/validation/plan keywords no longer steal development prompts. 6 regression cases; six-intent invariant kept. 49 tests green.

title: Fix model-failure detection in completeRewrite (F1)
description:
# PROBLEM

Critical. ModelRuntime.completeSimple() (installed 0.84.2) resolves with an AssistantMessage having content:[] and stopReason:"error" plus errorMessage on provider/auth/network/timeout failure; it never rejects (verified: dist/core/model-runtime.js:467, dist/api/lazy.js createSetupErrorMessage, dist/utils/event-stream.js result() is resolve-only). completeRewrite (src/app.mjs:350-367) therefore treats every real failure as "malformed output": it retries once (a second full model call, up to another 45s), then reports the misleading "model did not return an actionable <xtprompt> rewrite after one retry." The TimeoutError/AbortError->"timed out" branch (:362-364) and the generic "model request failed." branch (:365) are dead code against the real API; they fire only because the test harness mock throws. Real diagnostics (401, rate limit, network, timeout) never reach the user. Empirically confirmed: a call with no API key resolved with stopReason:"error", errorMessage:"No API key for provider: openai".

# SUCCESS

completeRewrite inspects the resolved message before retrying: a stopReason:"error" (or errorMessage present) result returns { error: "model request failed." } immediately, no retry, exit code 1, no model output leaked. Retry happens only when content exists but is not actionable (no sentinel, clarification-only, control bytes). The test harness mock is updated to mirror the real contract: failure scenarios return resolved {content:[], stopReason:"error"} messages instead of throwing, and the old throwing-based tests are replaced with equivalents that assert no-retry-on-real-failure and honest diagnostics.

# SCOPE

src/app.mjs (completeRewrite, completeOnce at 350-381), test/app.test.mjs (harness completeSimple mock + the failure-path tests at :184-211), README.md only if diagnostic wording changes.

# NON_GOALS

- No change to pi-coding-agent itself.
- No new timeout budget logic beyond the existing per-attempt 45s (a shared-budget question stays open; see epic open question).
- No change to the retry-once semantics for malformed output.

# CONSTRAINTS

- Real provider failures must be distinguishable from malformed output by inspecting the resolved message fields (stopReason/errorMessage), not by catching.
- Diagnostics stay secret-safe: never print errorMessage or the model body; the existing tests assert this.
- The mock in app.test.mjs must represent the real API contract so the suite tests the same path production uses; keep exact-request-count assertions (1 call on real failure, 2 on malformed-then-recovered).
- npm test and npm run test:coverage pass; coverage thresholds hold.

# VALIDATION

- [ ] New test: resolved {content:[], stopReason:"error"} response -> exactly 1 model call, exit 1, stderr "xtprompt: model request failed." (no retry, no model output).
- [ ] New test: timeout signal abort -> same no-retry, honest diagnostic path (or documented equivalence).
- [ ] Existing tests: malformed-first-then-valid still does exactly 2 calls; malformed-retry failure still exits 1 with the "not actionable" message; model-error tests updated to resolved-error mocks still assert no leak.
- [ ] Full suite + coverage run green.
- [ ] The dead-code branches (:362-365) are either reachable again or removed with comment explaining the contract.

# OUTPUT

Changed files list, before/after behavior table for failure scenarios, test output for the suite + coverage, note on which error branch is now reachable, residual risk: whether real providers honor the abort signal at 45s (unverified without a live call).
close_reason: F1 fixed: completeRewrite detects resolved stopReason:'error'/errorMessage before retry; returns generic 'model request failed.', exit 1, no leak, no retry. Harness mock mirrors real resolved-error contract; throwing-path tests converted; regression + TimeoutError tests added. 45 tests green.

title: xtprompt remediation: fix review findings in packages/xtprompt
description:
# PROBLEM

A deep review of packages/xtprompt (source, tests, installed dependency @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.84.2, live PTY experiments) found one critical defect and several major ones. The critical defect (F1): ModelRuntime.completeSimple() resolves with stopReason:"error" on provider/auth/network/timeout failure instead of rejecting, so completeRewrite never detects real failures, retries every failure once (doubling cost and latency up to 2x45s), and reports a misleading "model did not return an actionable rewrite" message; the timeout and generic failure diagnostics are dead code. The README's own usage examples fail: short concrete prompts are classified vague (F3), and planning requests contradict their own output contract (F2). Auto-intent misclassifies development prompts as planning (F8). These defects break normal use and error reporting of a released CLI.

# SUCCESS

Every finding from the review (F1-F17) is resolved or explicitly deferred with a tracked decision. completeRewrite detects real model failures on the first call, surfaces an honest diagnostic, and retries only malformed-but-valid output. The README usage examples produce the documented exit codes. Planning requests succeed on the first attempt. All tests pass (existing 43 plus new regression tests), coverage stays above the 80% thresholds, and the packed tarball still ships the four src files and README.

# SCOPE

packages/xtprompt only: src/app.mjs, src/cli.mjs, src/prompt.mjs, src/clipboard.mjs, test/ (prompt.test.mjs, app.test.mjs, clipboard.test.mjs, pty.test.mjs), README.md, package.json. The installed pi-coding-agent dependency is read-only reference, not modified.

# NON_GOALS

- No new CLI features or flags (no --api-key, no --list-models, no abort-on-SIGINT guarantee changes).
- No changes to the pi-coding-agent dependency or its call contract beyond what the caller must handle (checking stopReason/errorMessage is a caller-side fix).
- No support for extension-registered providers; README already documents they are not loaded.
- No changes outside packages/xtprompt (no xtrm core, no other packages).

# CONSTRAINTS

- Exit-code contract is preserved: 0 success, 1 runtime/model failure, 2 invalid input/options/context/model selection, 130 interactive Ctrl-C.
- Diagnostics must never include prompt text, resolved credentials, or model response bodies (existing tests enforce this; keep them green).
- No new runtime dependencies.
- Changes to the app.test.mjs harness (mock completeSimple must mirror the real resolved-error-message contract) land in the same change as the completeRewrite fix (T1) and are a precondition for T5 and T6, which share app.mjs/app.test.mjs.
- Each fix ships its own regression test; the suite must stay green at every step (npm test in packages/xtprompt).
- README claims and code must agree; where behavior is fixed, update README examples to prompts that pass.

# VALIDATION

- [ ] All child beads closed with evidence (test output, changed files, residual risks).
- [ ] Existing suite green after each fix; new regression tests cover each fixed finding.
- [ ] npm run test:coverage in packages/xtprompt passes the 80% line/branch/function thresholds.
- [ ] Piped README example `echo "analyze this failure" | xtprompt --intent analysis` exits 0 (or the README example is corrected deliberately and the new example verified).
- [ ] PTY smoke: interactive refine + :accept + Ctrl-C->130 still pass.
- [ ] npm pack --dry-run still ships src/ and README.md.
- [ ] No credential/prompt/body text in any diagnostic path (existing leak tests stay green).

# OUTPUT

At epic close, the orchestrator reports: per-child handoff summaries, the integration evidence (full test + coverage + PTY + pack runs), the list of findings resolved vs deferred (with tracking IDs for deferred), and residual risks (live model call behavior not exercised; CRLF emission by real providers unverified).

# REFERENCES

Findings F1-F17 from the xtprompt review of 2026-08-14 (in-session report). Source anchor points: src/app.mjs:350-381 (completeRewrite/completeOnce), src/app.mjs:188-193 (clarifyDraft), src/prompt.mjs:47-54 (isVagueDraft), src/prompt.mjs:19-24 (INTENT_RULES), src/prompt.mjs:136-140 + 36-43 (planning output contract vs BASE_RULES), src/cli.mjs:7-14 (ask), src/clipboard.mjs:4-15 (writeClipboard).

title: xtprompt returns clarification questions instead of rewritten prompts
description:
## Problem
The installed xtprompt CLI can emit a bare clarification question as its final successful output. Reproductions include `xtprompt "hello this is a test"` followed by clarification answer `test`, and a review request that returns only a question about package/build commands. The CLI must produce an actionable enhanced prompt, not answer the draft or ask further questions in model output.

## Acceptance criteria
- Add regression coverage for model responses that are only clarification questions.
- Strengthen the shared prompt contract or output validation so successful output is an actionable rewritten prompt.
- Preserve the existing single CLI clarification for vague TTY input.
- Verify both reported examples through authenticated smoke tests.
- Keep existing tests and coverage gates passing.
notes: Root cause: BASE_RULES and intent instructions told the model to clarify missing facts, while completeRewrite accepted every non-empty <xtprompt> block. Fix: require actionable rewrites, encode missing facts inside the prompt, detect one-line clarification-only questions, and retry once with an explicit correction. Verification: 20/20 tests pass; coverage 92.58% lines, 82.81% branches, 90.63% functions; syntax checks and npm audit pass; both user-reported live authenticated examples now return actionable prompts. GitNexus detect_changes found only the expected prompt-construction/rewrite flow.
close_reason: Fixed: xtprompt now rejects clarification-only model output, retries as an actionable rewrite, and both reported examples pass live smoke tests.

title: fix(service-knowledge): skill_activator decide() hard-blocks when the index is merely unimportable
description:
retrieve_evidence()'s docstring (skill_activator.py:182-184) states: 'available=False means the packaged index is not importable in this process (hook running standalone without the pip package) - that must NEVER block, only degrade to advisory. available=True, ok=False means a real retrieval failure (broken index) - that may block.'

decide() line 318 contradicts this: 'elif not retrieval.ok and not exempt:' blocks on ok==False without ever reading retrieval.available. The Retrieval.available field is dead code - nothing consumes it.

Observed in mercury-market-data: the PreToolUse hook is wired to system python3, which cannot import service_knowledge (only the pipx venv can), so every Write/Edit touching a registered territory was hard-denied with 'Retrieval failed: service-knowledge index not importable' - including edits to .gitignore and .claude/settings.json, which are not in any territory. That deadlocks the operator: the hook blocks the very edit that would repair the hook.

Fix: gate the block on 'retrieval.available and not retrieval.ok'; when available is False, return an advisory allow.

Secondary: territory matching attributed .gitignore and .claude/settings.json to serving-mcp-tools, whose territory is 'api/mcp_server.py, api/docstrings/**/*, api/toon.py, api/filtering.py'. Neither path matches those globs - investigate the fallback that picks a service when no glob matches.

title: fix(service-knowledge): make drift detection ref-based so isolated worktrees work
description:
drift_detector.py:250 selects drift with 'fp.stat().st_mtime > last_sync'. A fresh git worktree checkout restamps every file's mtime, so any isolated run reports the entire registered territory as drifted. Measured in mercury-market-data at one commit with identical content: 64 items in the live repo vs 166 in a worktree of the same HEAD.

Effect: xtrm-service-knowledge-reconcile.yaml had to be switched to worktree.enabled=false (it previously ran isolated and, combined with the tree being gitignored, silently reported ALIGNED against 64 real drift items).

Fix: select drift by comparing last_sync_ref..HEAD (git diff --name-only) instead of mtime, falling back to mtime only when last_sync_ref is empty/unresolvable. The service registry already stores last_sync_ref and service_knowledge_diff_scan.py already does ref-based diffing, so the machinery exists.

Acceptance: scan_drift() returns identical results in a repo and in a fresh worktree of the same HEAD; then re-enable worktree.enabled=true in the reconcile workflow.

- Evidence:
  - `packages/service-knowledge/src/service_knowledge/mcp/knowledge_get.py:28-37` accepts caller `skill_path`.
  - `packages/service-knowledge/src/service_knowledge/index/query.py:369-381` builds `Path(consumer_root) / skill_rel_path`, checks existence, then returns raw `read_text()` content.
  - No repo-containment check. No `SKILL.md` allowlist.
- Reachability/exploitability: Any MCP caller able to invoke `knowledge_get` can submit traversal or absolute path. `consumer_root` also caller-controlled through `mcp/_root.py:14-16`.
- Impact: Read MCP process-readable files, including secret/config files. Fallback bypasses indexed-document secret scrubbing.
- Recommended fix: Resolve candidate path; require `candidate.is_relative_to(root.resolve())`; require expected registered skill path or strict `.../SKILL.md` allowlist. Remove raw filesystem fallback; return only scrubbed indexed document.
- Verification after fix: Tests reject traversal, absolute paths, non-SKILL files, alternate `consumer_root`; confirm no raw secret reaches MCP response.

### SK-002 — Medium — Secret scrubber misses Discord webhook assignments (CWE-200)
- Evidence:
  - `packages/service-knowledge/src/service_knowledge/index/secrets.py:29-43` covers Slack webhook only, credential URLs, JWTs, tokens, generic assignment names.
  - Generic assignment matcher excludes webhook URL variable names.
  - `builder.py:131-169` stores scrubber output in SQLite/FTS; `query.py:340-349` returns stored text through MCP.
  - Existing test `index/tests/test_secrets.py:22-26` checks Discord-named variable paired with Slack URL, so Slack-specific rule masks missing Discord format coverage.
- Reachability/exploitability: Secret accidentally committed in indexed SKILL content, then queried through MCP/index.
- Impact: Bearer webhook credential persists in SQLite, FTS, evidence bundles, backups.
- Recommended fix: Add Discord webhook pattern and generic `*_WEBHOOK_URL` assignment coverage. Add regression test using Discord-shaped synthetic URL; assert absence from every searchable layer and MCP response.
- Verification after fix: Rebuild test index; scan `documents`, FTS, `sk_items`, MCP bundle for synthetic value.

title: Epic: service-skills reframe — deterministic verifier + evidence-first retrieval
description:
## PROBLEM

Two failure modes prove the current service-skills machinery ships operational-knowledge risk unchecked:

1. **Blast radius on rewrite**: reconcile.py + service-skills-sync specialist generate rewritten SKILL.md and write immediately — no fact-check, no citation extraction, no completeness verification. A single specialist run recently shipped a SKILL section with invented redaction-key set, wrong redaction literal, mis-labeled metric-label set. Wrong SKILL becomes ground truth for every future session.

2. **Consumption gap**: SKILLs are barely used. skill_activator.py fires a 'please read this' reminder AFTER the tool call the agent already committed to. Nothing in bead contracts, specialist prompts, or issue dispatch demands service context.

Research (~/dev/xtrm/docs/research/kb-knowledge-base-svc.md, 975 lines, cited SOTA + shipping systems) recommends two derived layers on top of existing SKILL.md/registry/machinery:
- **Claim verifier**: deterministic Python between LLM output and any write/commit/PR; explicit gate lattice (INVALID / CONFLICT / EVIDENCE_RACE / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK / PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES / PASS); PASS != auto-merge on day one.
- **Evidence-first retrieval**: per-repo SQLite FTS5 index + narrow read-only MCP tools; no answer() endpoint.

Given the scale + coherence of the reframe, machinery elevates to a first-class xtrm package: **service-knowledge**, home ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/. **Independent lifecycle**: its own CLI (`service-knowledge install|update|status|migrate|remove`) — NOT routed through `xt update --apply`. Rename from 'service-skills' → 'service-knowledge' reflects the reframe target.

## SUCCESS

At epic close:
- Auto-reconcile + specialist runs cannot ship SKILL with invented literals, wrong metric-label sets, invented env vars, or falsely-complete lists — verifier blocks BEFORE atomic_write.
- Every bead touching a registered territory receives an evidence bundle at dispatch; Write/Edit in registered territory blocks when bundle can't be built.
- SKILL.md remains authoring surface; registry stays source of truth.
- Machinery ships as first-class xtrm package (service-knowledge v0.6.0) with own CLI, own release cadence, own CHANGELOG.
- **vaultctl is a package dependency** (~/dev/vaultctl provides SQLite/FTS5/BM25 substrate — 897 LOC of proven store layer we don't rewrite). service-knowledge adds only the domain-specific extensions (items with kind=service|section|claim|probe|conflict, citations, retrieval_events, index_state).
- **mercury-infra is the PoC consumer** (17 services, richest fixture set). 6 other service-hosting mercury repos adopt when operator triggers each — no forced-wave.
- **~/dev/core and ~/dev/specialists are NOT consumers**. They are xtrm tooling repos, not service hosts. Nothing to index there.
- Federated cross-repo query via ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json enables devops-agent-dispatched-from-infra to touch sibling stacks without centralized DB.
- 80-150-case labeled eval corpus + telemetry proves retrieval precision/recall, stale-claim escape rate, verifier FP/FN rates.

## SCOPE

**Package home**: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/ — independent, own CLI, own versioning

**Package CLI** (new):
- `service-knowledge install` — first-time install in a consumer repo
- `service-knowledge update` — pull latest package version into consumer
- `service-knowledge status` — report installed version + index health + drift
- `service-knowledge migrate` — rename/schema migration (used in PR0 for the service-skills → service-knowledge flip)
- `service-knowledge remove` — uninstall (for consumer repos that deprecate)

**Consumer path** (in each of 7 service-hosting mercury repos): .xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/ (renamed from service-skills/)

**Per-repo derived index**: .xtrm/cache/service-knowledge.sqlite (NOT .beads/)

**Cross-repo federation surface**: ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json (user-scoped)

**Consumer repos (7 service-hosting mercury only)**:
- mercury-infra (PoC #1)
- mercury-market-data
- mercury-darth-feedor  
- mercury-treasury-cb
- mercury-quant
- mercury-sierra-vps
- mercury-website

**NOT consumers**: ~/dev/core, ~/dev/specialists, ~/dev/xtrm, ~/dev/xtmux, ~/dev/vaultctl — xtrm tooling repos, no services to index.

**Dependencies**:
- vaultctl (as a Python package dep) — provides SQLite/FTS5/BM25/indexer/search/graph substrate

**Docs home**: ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md

## NON_GOALS

- Not routed through `xt update --apply` — service-knowledge has its OWN CLI (`service-knowledge update`). Independent lifecycle.
- ~/dev/core and ~/dev/specialists are NOT installed — they host xtrm tooling, not services
- No new database service (Postgres, vector DB, external store)
- No LLM in retrieval hot path or as gate arbiter; no LLM-panel majority vote
- No auto-merge on PASS in initial rollout (canary decision in PR5b)
- No single centralized ~/.xtrm/knowledge.sqlite union DB — federated over per-repo indexes
- No embeddings (deferred until BM25 recall failure measured)
- No replacement of registry, SKILL.md, or Dolt-backed bd memory
- No general-purpose organizational KB, Slack connector, or auto-remediation
- No simultaneous rewrite of all 17 shipped SKILLs — semantic-markers migration is progressive
- No docs/ inside package on day one — add when first substantive doc lands
- No forced-wave migration of 6 other mercury repos in PR0 — operator triggers each when ready
- **Don't reimplement what vaultctl already ships**: schema.sql, indexer, search, BM25 tokenization, link resolution, in-degree graph, CLI-JSON scaffolding

## CONSTRAINTS

- Machinery lives in ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/; never migrate back to core.
- Package has independent CLI, independent versioning, independent release. NOT bundled with any other xtrm package's update cadence.
- Consumer set is ONLY service-hosting mercury repos. If a new mercury service-host repo lands, add to consumer list; core/specialists/tooling repos NEVER become consumers.
- vaultctl is a hard dep; service-knowledge does not reimplement its store layer. Domain schema extensions attach on top.
- Registry stays source of truth for service ↔ territory; index at .xtrm/cache/service-knowledge.sqlite is rebuildable projection.
- Deterministic before LLM at every gate; LLM steps produce advisory output only.
- Provenance model NOT ADD-only: active/superseded/invalidated + append-only history.
- Semantic markers hard-protected everywhere.
- Blocking hooks scoped tightly: Write/Edit registered territory + high-risk mutating Bash. Read/Glob/Grep never block.
- Package versioning: v0.1.0 baseline after PR0; +minor per merged PR (PR1→v0.2.0, PR2→v0.3.0, PR3→v0.4.0, PR4→v0.5.0, PR5a→v0.6.0, PR5b→v0.7.0). Reserve v1.0.0 for canary auto-merge activation.
- Logging/telemetry: every retrieval + verifier decision emits structured event to .xtrm/state/service-knowledge/events.jsonl. No secrets. No raw payloads.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Package released at v0.6.0 (or v0.7.0 with PR5b)
- [ ] `service-knowledge --help` works standalone; NOT routed through `xt update`
- [ ] vaultctl imported as dep; service-knowledge stores 5-table extension (items/citations/conflicts/retrieval_events/index_state) as an attached DB or migration
- [ ] All 7 mercury service-host repos CAN install (`service-knowledge install`); mercury-infra IS installed as wave-1
- [ ] core + specialists + xtrm + xtmux + vaultctl are NOT installed (validation: `ls ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/` returns 'not found')
- [ ] Deterministic verifier catches all 3 failure classes from observed api-gateway/runners regression — golden fixture per class
- [ ] reconcile.py refuses atomic_write on CONFLICT/INVALID; draft-only PR on INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK
- [ ] Every bead touching a registered territory attaches evidence_bundle_id + evidence_hash
- [ ] Write/Edit in registered territory blocks when retrieval fails (with clear override path)
- [ ] Federated query via ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json returns ranked results across ≥2 stacks with per-repo provenance
- [ ] Labeled eval corpus (≥80 cases): routing precision ≥ 0.8, retrieval precision@5 ≥ 0.6, stale-claim escape rate ≤ 0.05
- [ ] Verifier FP ≤ 0.05, FN ≤ 0.10
- [ ] Semantic-block protection: 100% preserved across every regeneration path
- [ ] Post-merge reindex ≤ 60s on all 7 consumers
- [ ] ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md links resolve

## OUTPUT

At epic close, orchestrator publishes:
- Per-PR summary (merged SHA, key changes, coverage delta, package version)
- service-knowledge v0.6+ CHANGELOG
- Verifier golden-fixture report + regression classes
- Eval corpus stats
- Retrieval telemetry snapshot (7d after PR4)
- Federated-query smoke transcript (≥2 stacks)
- Wave-1 install evidence (mercury-infra); wave-2..7 tracking issue for on-operator-trigger installs
- Residual risks + follow-up beads (residual LLM critic if verifier FN > 0.10; session cache if activator latency > 200ms; centralized DB triggers; per-role ACL; remaining 8 claim types)
- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md updated with the shipped user manual

## REFERENCES

- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/research/kb-knowledge-base-svc.md — the 975-line deep research doc (§1-§7)
- ~/dev/vaultctl/ — SQLite/FTS5/BM25 substrate package (dep)
- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/ — home for operator-facing service-knowledge docs
- /tmp/deep-research-prompt-svc-skills.md — prompt that produced the research
- ~/dev/core/docs/design/memory-system-r6g.md — adjacent design (shared plumbing: FTS5, provenance)
- ~/dev/core/docs/service-skills-auto-reconcile.md — current Phase A + B runbook (migrates under the package)
- Sibling bead xtrm-y0tdg (Repo skills layout v2) — layout concern, keep separate
- Sibling bead infra-wtd1 (orphan-scan) — orphan-detection lane; ships in parallel; its service_skill_orphan_scan.py also moves into the package via PR0

## EXECUTION MODEL

All 6 (or 7 with PR5b split) PRs dispatch via specialists per /multiplexing + /using-specialists:
`sp run <specialist> --bead xtrm-56flm.N --worktree` on each. Parallelization:
- Wave 1: PR0 (blocks all) — solo
- Wave 2: PR1 || PR3 (both blocked-by PR0 only)
- Wave 3: PR2 (blocked-by PR1) || PR4 (blocked-by PR3)
- Wave 4: PR5a (blocked-by all impl) || PR5b (blocked-by PR5a for measurement inputs, else standalone)

Coordinator dispatches, monitors panes per /multiplexing message-send + safe-send-pointer, applies gate5 (reviewer PASS + merge) per /using-specialists rule #9. Target: ship in ~3-4 days with 2-3 waves running concurrent workers.

title: Reconcile collaborator identity, runtime delivery and observability surfaces
description:
## PROBLEM

The collaborator design has a strong external GitHub bot identity but largely collapses internal runtime identity into Specialists jobs/processes and operator `docker exec` surfaces. It also predates the accepted separation between immutable Channels semantics and process-state-dependent runtime delivery. Without correction, audit/provenance can confuse the credentialed GitHub principal, logical XTRM actor, assignment participant and concrete execution attempt.

## SUCCESS

Sections 3 and 9 distinguish external principal identity from XTRM actor/assignment/participant/execution/runtime lineage, and document how bridge `job_id`/process identifiers relate to the durable execution envelope. Operator observability exposes runtime execution state, evidence and Channels attention/delivery in addition to current `sp ps`/`sp feed` bridge commands. Semantic messages remain Channels-owned; scheduler/runtime owns eligibility, delivery attempts and processing receipts.

## SCOPE

- `docs/devops/mercury-devops-collaborator.md` Section 3 lifecycle/identity description
- Section 9 operator observability
- adjacent messaging/notification statements that conflate semantic message with process delivery

## NON_GOALS

- Do not implement Channels storage or Console/Agent Workspace.
- Do not require every external principal field on every low-level runtime event.
- Do not replace the dedicated GitHub bot identity or weaken credential isolation.
- Do not make terminal panes/processes the source of runtime identity.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The design must be able to resolve/join at least `principal_id` where applicable, `actor_id`, `assignment_id`, `participant_id`, `execution_id`, `attempt`, `parent_execution_id`, bridge `job_id`, `runtime_session_id`, `generation` and `authority_ref`.
- Authority-bearing sender identity is runtime-derived/validated; message body text cannot impersonate another actor/execution.
- `ChannelMessage -> DeliveryIntent -> DeliveryAttempt -> ProcessingReceipt` is the semantic/runtime split; delivered is not processed.
- Current `docker exec ... sp ps/feed/result` commands may remain documented as bridge observability, not the target ontology.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] GitHub bot principal identity is explicitly separated from internal XTRM actor/execution identity.
- [ ] `job_id` is documented as a bridge/current runtime identifier rather than the complete durable identity.
- [ ] Parent/child/recovery lineage can be joined through execution/session/generation fields.
- [ ] Channels author identity is runtime-derived and body-not-authority is preserved.
- [ ] Semantic message state is separated from runtime delivery/processing state.
- [ ] Section 9 exposes evidence, execution state, attention/pending-delivery and recovery-relevant identity in addition to process/job views.

## OUTPUT

Doc diff and identity/observability crosswalk covering external principal, XTRM logical/workflow identity, runtime execution identity, current bridge identifiers, Channels delivery state and evidence locations.

title: Reconcile collaborator recovery and GC around durable executions and owned resources
description:
## PROBLEM

Sections 6-7 equate container restart with orphaned `running` Specialists jobs and describe recovery/GC as process/job cleanup plus branch deletion in container-local shell. The accepted runtime model treats an execution as a durable object with lineage, runtime session identity and generation; restart may require resume, reconciliation, lease expiry or terminalization rather than unconditional stop. GC must likewise prove ownership and terminality before deleting resources.

## SUCCESS

The collaborator design describes recovery as classification of durable execution state and owned resources. Restart recovery distinguishes terminal, resumable, orphaned, lease-expired, `uncertain` and irrecoverable cases; replay/snapshot/generation semantics are referenced where applicable; cleanup releases only resources whose ownership and terminality are proven. Git/worktree cleanup, runtime execution/session cleanup, Specialists workflow evidence, Channels delivery state and log/forensic retention remain separate concerns with separate evidence.

## SCOPE

## SUCCESS

The document preserves the useful three-layer freshness policy while expressing event handling as a durable workflow/runtime boundary: event admission and idempotency first, deterministic scheduler intent second, eligibility/lease resolution before mutable execution, and an explicit completed/failed-safe/`uncertain` outcome for side effects such as rebase/push/PR actions. - Do not authorize autonomous conflict resolution.

- Preferred conceptual flow: `event -> durable admission/idempotency -> scheduler intent -> lease/eligibility -> execution/delivery -> recorded outcome`.

title: bootstrap.get_registry_path: probe <pack>/service-skills/service-registry.json (drift detector L0)
description:
## Problem

`bootstrap.get_registry_path()` at `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py:118-155`
resolves the registry via 5 probes (env var → root symlink → pack root → legacy → create-at). The
pack-root probe (line 144) checks `<pack>/service-registry.json` only.

Mercury infra and other Mercury repos materialize the registry one level deeper at
`<pack>/service-skills/service-registry.json` (the service-skills SKILL's own
directory holds both the SKILL.md and the registry it owns). bootstrap.get_registry_path
falls through all probes and returns a non-existent create-at path. load_registry()
returns {"services": {}} and the drift detector scans 0 services in a permanent
silent-fail state.

## Cross-repo context

Discovered while wiring drift detection in mercury-infra (bead infra-j2v8, closed
with option-A symlink workaround). Same defect affects every Mercury project that
holds a service-skills pack — currently mercury-infra + the 8 other repos that
adopted the pack via xt update.

## Resolution (additive, non-breaking)

Add a 6th probe between lines 145 and 147:

    if pack is not None:
        pack_reg = pack / "service-registry.json"
        if pack_reg.exists():
            return pack_reg
        # NEW: probe the canonical service-skills subdir.
        ss_reg = pack / "service-skills" / "service-registry.json"
        if ss_reg.exists():
            return ss_reg

Then update the create-at fallback (line 153) to use the service-skills subdir
when it exists as a directory (so newly bootstrapped projects land at the right
place).

## Acceptance

- Smoke from mercury-infra: load_registry returns 15 services (was 0)
- Smoke from xtrm-tools itself: no regression in existing test suite
- No envvar / config change required by consumers

## Out of scope

Deeper drift detector debt (L1 silent-skip / L2 last_sync vs last_sync_ref / L3 mtime
vs git SHA) — separate beads to be filed because L2 requires alignment with
dev/specialists unitAI-4zask shape decision.

## References

- cross-repo discovered-from: mercury-infra bead `infra-j2v8` (closed via option-A symlink workaround)
- related: dev/specialists `unitAI-4zask` (script-specialist post-merge pipeline shape decision)
- code: .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py:118-155

title: Phase B — mcpq CLI subcommands: list-tools, describe, call (typed args)
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase A shipped the foundation (protocol + transport + .mcpq.json + `mcpq servers`). The Phase B CLI subcommands `list-tools`, `describe`, and `call` are currently stubs that print "implemented in Phase B". This bead implements them with full ergonomic UX (human + json output) and the typed-args marshaling for `call`. Covers original beads xtrm-2m3.4 (read subcommands: list-tools, describe) and xtrm-2m3.5 (action subcommand: call with typed args).

## SUCCESS

Working subcommands end-to-end against the live sidecars on `mercury_platform`:
- `mcpq <server> list-tools` returns the live tool list (no hardcoded schema, fresh discovery every call). Human-readable default (table-ish) and `--json` raw output.
- `mcpq <server> describe <tool>` prints the input schema (typed args, required fields, defaults) plus tool title/description. `--json` flag supported.
- `mcpq <server> call <tool> [--arg key=value ...] [--json]` marshals typed args into a JSON-RPC `tools/call` payload, executes via MCPClient, renders the result. Type coercion: `key=value` defaults to string; `key:int=42`, `key:float=3.14`, `key:bool=true|false|1|0`, `key:json={"x":1}` for explicit typing.

End-to-end live proofs:
- `mcpq prometheus list-tools` returns 6 tools.
- `mcpq prometheus describe mercury_execute_query` shows schema with `query: string` (required) and optional `time` etc.
- `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job="prometheus"}'` returns a vector result with at least one sample with `value=1`.
- `mcpq grafana list-tools` returns 49 tools.
- `mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards` shows input schema.
- `mcpq grafana call search_dashboards` returns ≥10 dashboards.

## SCOPE (MODIFY EXISTING + 1 NEW FILE)

**Existing files in `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/` — modify ONLY these:**
- `cli.py` — replace `_cmd_stub` calls for `list-tools`, `describe`, `call` with real implementations. Keep argparse subparsers as-is; wire them to new functions.
- `client.py` — minor: ensure `call_tool` returns a useful result envelope; add helper to convert `tools/list` result to the same shape regardless of server flavor.
- `protocol.py` — only if needed for `call_tool` envelope already exists in Phase A — likely no change.

**New file allowed:**
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/render.py` — output rendering helpers (human-readable tool list, schema pretty-printer, result rendering). Pure functions, no I/O. ~80 lines max.
- `packages/mcpq/src/mcpq/args.py` — typed-arg parser for the `--arg key:type=value` syntax. Pure function `parse_args(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]`. ~50 lines max.

## NON_GOALS

- Tests (Phase D / xtrm-2m3.d).
- Skill body or expanded README beyond what already exists (Phase C).
- mercury-infra `.mcpq.json` integration (Phase D).
- stdio transport, multi-server batch, result caching.
- Schema validation against tool input schemas client-side (server is the validator; we just pass through).
- New third-party deps on the call path.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Python 3.10+ stdlib only on call path.
- Reuse Phase A `MCPClient` / `ServerSpec` / `validation` helpers — do NOT bypass `validate_url` / `validate_header_value` / `validate_container_name`.
- Telemetry MUST emit on every subcommand (success and error). Use `log_invocation(server, subcommand, tool, duration_ms, outcome)` — fill `tool` for describe/call, leave empty for list-tools.
- Human-readable output format hints:
  - `list-tools` default: one tool per line, `<name>  <title or description short>`, sorted alphabetically by name.
  - `describe` default: name, title, description, then `Args:` indented `  <field>  <type>  <required|optional> [default=<x>]  <description>`.
  - `call` default: pretty-print result (JSON with 2-space indent) — MCP `tools/call` results typically have `content: [{type: "text", text: "..."}]`; if so, print the joined text content; if not, fall back to full JSON.
- `--json` flag on all three subcommands emits raw JSON to stdout — no human formatting.
- Argument syntax for `call`:
  - `--arg name=value` → string
  - `--arg name:int=42` → int(value)
  - `--arg name:float=3.14` → float(value)
  - `--arg name:bool=true` → True (accept true/false/1/0/yes/no, case-insensitive); raises ValueError otherwise
  - `--arg name:json='{"x":1}'` → json.loads(value)
  - Raises clear error on type-conversion failure: "invalid value for arg <name> as <type>: <err>"
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 user error (missing server, missing tool, bad args), 2 transport/server error.
- Errors go to stderr; telemetry one-line JSON also stderr (existing pattern). stdout for results only.

## VALIDATION

After implementation, in the executor worktree (it has the Phase A merged + the .venv-mcpq from prior):

1. `pip install -e packages/mcpq` clean.
2. `mcpq --help` shows all 4 subcommands (no "phase B stub" text).
3. From `packages/mcpq/`:
   - `mcpq prometheus list-tools` → paste full output (should list 6 mercury_-prefixed tools).
   - `mcpq prometheus list-tools --json | python3 -c "import sys,json; t=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(t), 'tools'); print(t[0]['name'])"` → confirms json output is a list of tool dicts.
   - `mcpq prometheus describe mercury_execute_query` → paste output, must show `query` (string, required) at minimum.
   - `mcpq prometheus call mercury_health_check` → paste raw output (this is the safe no-arg call).
   - `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job="prometheus"}'` → paste output; check it contains either result value=1 or a clear error explaining metric not exposed (label the outcome accordingly).
4. From `packages/mcpq/`:
   - `mcpq grafana list-tools` → paste tool count + first 5 names.
   - `mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards` → paste output.
   - `mcpq grafana call search_dashboards` → paste outcome (dashboard count if successful, or error if the grafana token lacks permission).
5. Telemetry: `mcpq prometheus list-tools 2>&1 1>/dev/null` → grep that telemetry JSON line contains `"server":"prometheus", "subcommand":"list-tools"`.
6. Error path: `mcpq prometheus call nonexistent_tool` → clear error message + nonzero exit code.
7. Argument typing: `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_range_query --arg query=up --arg start:int=1700000000 --arg end:int=1700000600 --arg step=15` → paste outcome (proves int coercion works).
8. Bad arg syntax: `mcpq prometheus call x --arg badform` → clear error.

## OUTPUT (handoff schema)

- Changed files list (modifications + new files)
- Pasted raw outputs for ALL VALIDATION steps 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
- Confirm NO `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` paths in `git show --name-only HEAD`

- Confirm telemetry still emits on EVERY subcommand
- Residual risks (e.g., behaviors not yet covered, server-specific quirks)
- Machine-readable block (as per per-turn handoff schema)

## REFERENCES

- Phase A shipped in 2ac44b4. The mcpq package is on main at packages/mcpq/. Self-test config at packages/mcpq/.mcpq.json. Phase A used .venv-mcpq at the worktree root.
- MCP spec tools/call: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification — request envelope `{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}}`; response result envelope `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"..."}], "isError":boolean}` or structuredContent for typed.
- Live sidecars on mercury_platform: infra-grafana-mcp (49 tools), infra-prometheus-mcp (6 mercury_* tools).
- Phase A noise filter: gitignore the executor's `.venv-mcpq`, `.smoke/`, `__pycache__/` and explicitly exclude any `.claude/` or `.codex/` paths from the commit.

### F-1 — SSRF: no scheme/host allowlist on outbound URL
- **Severity:** medium
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery

- **Impact:** Cloud-metadata exfil, internal-network probing, local-file read inside the docker-exec target container. Combined with F-4 (no container-name validation), pivot is feasible.

- **Verification after fix:** unit test with `http://169.254.169.254/`, `file:///etc/passwd`, `http://10.0.0.1/admin` — all should raise `TransportError` before any network I/O.

- **Severity:** medium
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-755 Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions / CWE-20 Input Validation

  2. - **Severity:** low
- **Category/CWE:** CWE-77 / CWE-862 Missing Authorization
- **Evidence:** `config.py:28-33` `ServerSpec.proxy_container` does `self.via.split(":", 1)[1]` with no validation. `transport.py:80` passes it directly as argv element to `docker exec`. title: Phase A — mcpq foundation: scaffold + protocol client + via-mode dispatch
description:
## PROBLEM

xtrm-2m3 epic requires a brand-new Python package at `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/` that bridges Docker-network-only MCP sidecars to host-side discovery and invocation. This bead covers the foundation: package scaffold (xtrm-2m3.1) + MCP protocol client with .mcpq.json discovery (xtrm-2m3.2) + via-mode dispatch supporting `host` and `docker:<container>` (xtrm-2m3.3). Without this foundation, no CLI surface or skill work can begin. title: security-auditor: per-session shell history isolation
description:
## PROBLEM
Shell hooks write one global state file shared by every terminal; xts therefore sees recent commands from any open session, leaking cross-terminal context (audit finding #12) and racing concurrent shells.

## SUCCESS
Each interactive shell exports a stable XTS_SESSION_ID (pid+tty) and writes state.<id>.json / cmds.<id>.txt; xts reads only its inherited session file; sessions without the hook fall back to the legacy global paths; session files older than 7 days are pruned by the hook; concurrent terminals are isolated (verified live with two tmux panes).

## SCOPE
packages/xts/src/history/hook.bash, hook.zsh, src/history/shell.mjs, README privacy note, test/shell.test.mjs.

## NON_GOALS
No cross-terminal aggregation mode; no daemon/cleanup process.

## CONSTRAINTS
Session id sanitized against path traversal; PRD §10 silence preserved; legacy no-id paths unchanged for compatibility; SCRUTINY: medium.

## VALIDATION
Unit: id-specific paths, traversal sanitization, fallback, prune logic. Live: two tmux panes with distinct markers prove mutual isolation and correct inheritance.

## OUTPUT
Diff, unit+live evidence.
close_reason: Per-session isolation shipped and live-verified with two concurrent tmux zsh sessions: each exports a stable XTS_SESSION_ID ($$), writes private state.<id>.json / cmds.<id>.txt (0700/0600 preserved), prunes >7-day-old session files, and xts inherits the id so it reads only its own terminal — pane A saw only ISO-MARKER-ALPHA, pane B only ISO-MARKER-BRAVO. Key discovery: zsh fc-based capture is inherently cross-terminal when history sharing is enabled (shared ~/.zsh_history imports surface other terminals via fc -ln -1), so the zsh hook now captures via add-zsh-hook preexec ($1 = literal command line of THIS shell); bash keeps fc since bash does not mid-session import. Read side sanitizes the id against path traversal and falls back to legacy global paths when no id is set. Tests: shell 15/15 incl. per-session path matrix, preset-id hook writes for bash+zsh, privacy/mode rerun; cli+prompt 36/36.

title: executor: stop pipe-mode inspections of the wrong directory
description:
## PROBLEM
`ls /tmp/ | xts "how many files, size per folder"` made the model run du/find in XTS launch cwd (~/dev/xtrm) and report unrelated folders, ignoring that the stdin evidence listed /tmp contents. The prompt never distinguishes the bash working directory from the subject of piped evidence.

## SUCCESS
System prompt states bash runs in the [shell context] cwd and that questions/piped stdin may refer to files elsewhere, which must be inspected by absolute path. Live repro answers about /tmp, not the launch dir. Budget stays under 200 estimated tokens.

## SCOPE
packages/xts/src/prompt.mjs (+ optional stdin block label), test/prompt.test.mjs.

## NON_GOALS
No cwd switching, no new flags.

## CONSTRAINTS
Prompt stays small; SCRUTINY: low.

## VALIDATION
prompt suite green; live rerun of the exact failing command inspects /tmp.

## OUTPUT
Diff and before/after evidence.
close_reason: Root cause: piped evidence carried no subject framing, so the model ran du/find in its own cwd and reported unrelated folders; a system-prompt-only rule made it notice the mismatch but not act on it. Fix is two-layer: SYSTEM_PROMPT states bash runs in the [shell context] cwd which may differ from the question subject (inspect by absolute path), and buildUserMessage stdin block now declares piped input as the SUBJECT of the request, instructing bash-tool inspection by absolute path — instruction adjacent to the data proved decisive. Live repro of `ls /tmp/ | xts "how many files, size per folder"` now inspects /tmp via bash and reports 2151 entries / 105 MB with per-directory sizes. Prompt ~190 estimated tokens (under 200 budget); prompt suite 10/10 with updated envelope assertions; cli+prompt+shell combined 49/49.

title: debugger: handle EPIPE and require TTY stdout for interactive mode
description:
## PROBLEM
Running `xts | ls` leaves stdout as a pipe; interactive mode starts the alt-screen TUI against it and crashes with an unhandled EPIPE stack trace when the pipe consumer exits. One-shot streaming has the same exposure (e.g. piping through head).

## SUCCESS
Interactive mode refuses to start unless BOTH stdin and stdout are TTYs, with a clear stderr message and exit 1. A process-level EPIPE guard makes late pipe closes on stdout harmless (exit quietly) instead of throwing; other stdout errors still surface.

## SCOPE
packages/xts/src/cli.mjs (guard + interactive check), focused test.

## NON_GOALS
No changes to pi-tui; no new modes.

## CONSTRAINTS
EPIPE handler ignores only errno -32/EPIPE and rethrows everything else; SCRUTINY: low.

## VALIDATION
Subprocess regression spawning cli with piped stdout asserts clean exit 1 + message (no stack trace); focused suites green.

## OUTPUT
Diff, test evidence.
close_reason: Fixed `xts | something` crash. Interactive now requires TTY on both stdin and stdout via exported missingInteractiveTtys() seam: piped-stdout repro (pty stdin + pipe stdout, the exact user scenario) exits 1 with `xts: interactive session requires a TTY on stdout. Did you mean: command | xts "question"?` — no stack trace. Process-level stdout EPIPE handler makes late consumer closes (`xts "q" | head`) exit quietly; non-EPIPE errors rethrow. Tests: cli 26/26 including a guard matrix covering both/neither/each side missing.

title: executor: make shell-hook installation durable and default
description:
## PROBLEM
Command-history context stays dormant unless users manually wire the hook into their rc; the operator wants hook enablement to be a durable default for every install/update, and wants it enabled now.

## SUCCESS
`xts shellhook` emits pure hook code safe for eval (usage instructions move to --help/README); an idempotent postinstall appends a marked, silent eval line to the detected rc ($SHELL: zsh->~/.zshrc else ~/.bashrc); re-runs are no-ops; XTS_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL or CI skips; install never fails on hook errors; existing machines get the line added once.

## SCOPE

## NON_GOALS
No fish/PowerShell; no hook auto-uninstall; no changes to hook internals.

## CONSTRAINTS
PRD §10 silence preserved; marker-comment idempotency; postinstall catches everything and exits 0. SCRUTINY: medium.

## VALIDATION
cli tests green incl. updated shellhook expectations; postinstall unit check with temp HOME adds line once; real rc gets exactly one marker block; fresh interactive shell produces state.json with recent commands.

## OUTPUT
Diffs, test output, rc evidence, live state.json sample.
close_reason: Durable default hook install shipped and enabled live. shellhook now prints pure hook code safe for eval (instructions moved to `xts shellhook --help`); scripts/postinstall.mjs runs on npm install/link, appending a marker-commented `eval "$(xts shellhook)"` to the $SHELL-matched rc (zsh->~/.zshrc, else ~/.bashrc), idempotent on rerun, skipped under XTS_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL or CI, best-effort exit 0 always. title: debugger: investigate packages/xts full-suite npm test host crash
description:
## PROBLEM
Running `npm test` (node --test over all files) in packages/xts crashes or wedges the orchestrator host tool, while every focused per-file suite passes (model/runtime/ui/cli 61/61; safety 43/43; pipe 25/25 at last runs). Suspected cause class: a TTY/PTY-grabbing test, runaway child process, or resource exhaustion under node --test parallelism on this host.

## SUCCESS
Identify the exact offending test/behavior, fix or isolate it (e.g. serial execution, child cleanup, PTY guard), so the full suite runs to completion without side effects on the invoking process.

## SCOPE
packages/xts/test/**, package.json test script only as needed.

## NON_GOALS
No production source changes unless the test exposes a real bug.

## CONSTRAINTS
Investigate via isolated single-file runs and timeouts first; never invoke the full suite from the coordinator context. SCRUTINY: medium.

## VALIDATION
Full suite completes with exit code and summary captured in a background/logged process; no hang; focused suites stay green.

## OUTPUT
Root cause, changed files, evidence of a clean full-suite run.
close_reason: Root cause identified: no product or test defect. Full packages/xts suite passes 129/129 (exit 0, ~5s) when run in an isolated background process; the coordinator-context crashes reproduced only when npm test was invoked through the orchestrator tool harness.
