title: Tests, performance measurement, and acceptance-criteria audit
description:
## PROBLEM

PRD §18 requires performance metrics (cold/warm startup, time-to-TUI, prompt/tool token counts, peak RSS) and PRD §24 lists 27 acceptance criteria that must each be verifiable. The per-task tests cover seams; this task owns the integrated verification surface.

## SUCCESS

- test/perf.mjs: measures cold process startup, warm startup, time to first visible TUI (interactive smoke via pty), system-prompt token count (heuristic), tool-schema token count, peak RSS (process.memoryUsage / /usr/bin/time); prints a table; assertions: startup overhead substantially below typical model latency (target: full non-model startup < 1.5s, interactive TUI < 2s)
- test/acceptance.md: checklist mapping each of the 27 PRD §24 criteria to its verification evidence (test name / smoke command / manual check), with status per criterion
- test/e2e.mjs (or shell script): smoke suite — xts --help, xts shellhook output, config round trip, model inventory json, one-shot answer (live model if available, else documented skip), pipe mode, truncation notice, xts run safe/dangerous/deny paths, redaction checks; skips live-model checks when no authenticated model
- Every acceptance criterion has either automated evidence or a documented manual check with exact commands

## SCOPE

- packages/xts/test/perf.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/test/acceptance.md (new)
- packages/xts/test/e2e.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/README.md (update: verification section)

## NON_GOALS

- No CI wiring beyond the package test script (repo has no per-package CI requirement)
- No publishing setup

## CONSTRAINTS

- Perf script must not require network/auth (measures only XTS initialization); uses child_process spawn + process.hrtime
- Acceptance doc must map criteria 1-27 exactly (PRD §24) and mark each verified / not-verified / manual with evidence path
- e2e smoke must exit non-zero on failure; live-model steps skip gracefully with SKIP reason when no model available
- Do not modify implementation modules except fixing bugs found (report via OUTPUT)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] perf.mjs runs and prints metrics table; numbers recorded in acceptance.md
- [ ] acceptance.md covers all 27 criteria with evidence
- [ ] e2e.mjs passes on this machine (live-model steps SKIP or pass)
- [ ] `npm test` green (all suites)
- [ ] README verification section updated

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: none new
- Installed deps: none new
- Stdlib: node:child_process, node:process, node:fs
- New dep candidate: none
- Roll it: yes — final verification task

## OUTPUT

perf metrics table, acceptance.md with 27/27 status, e2e smoke output, README verification section.
close_reason: All deliverables complete and independently reviewed. test/perf.mjs measures the real cli.mjs startup path via PTY: cold 61-64ms, warm full-process mean ~54-60ms, first visible TUI ~0.9s (ANSI-stripped detection), Enter-to-first-streamed-answer 1.6-2.0s including model latency, prompt 89 tokens, schema 128 tokens, RSS ~47MB — init overhead far below model latency per PRD §18. test/e2e.mjs: 14/14 genuine smokes verified by reviewer (PTY retained-answer with prompt-absent string, two-session persistence codeword recall in isolated XTS_STATE_DIR, dangerous-command no-exec sentinel, delayed bare/explicit pipes, live-model one-shot). test/acceptance.md maps all 27 PRD §24 criteria with honest statuses; reviewer spot-checked 1,5,6,9,16,18,21,23 confirmed, 26 now fully evidenced after perf rework. README verification section updated. Full suite 131/131 in isolated run. Reviewer PARTIAL findings (perf path completeness, stale metrics, bad criterion-19 reference, stale .7.3 note) all fixed and reproduced.

title: Runtime + CLI wiring — AgentSession integration, modes, persistence
description:
## PROBLEM

PRD §12/§20: the pieces (model, context, stdin, prompt, safety, TUI) must integrate into a slim AgentSession runtime behind the four CLI modes (interactive, one-shot, pipe, run) with conversation persistence and a closed resource surface. This is the final wiring task.

## SUCCESS

- src/runtime.mjs: `createXtsSession({ model, cwd, tools })` — createAgentSession with: explicit model, tools: ["bash"] (+ custom bash tool through the safety gate), closed resource loader (no extensions/skills/prompt templates/context files), SettingsManager.inMemory or minimal, SessionManager persistence (per-PRD §17.2 evaluation; default SessionManager.create(cwd) for conversation history continuity), thinkingLevel off (fast) or settings-based
- Closed surface verified: resourceLoader returns empty extensions/skills/prompts/themes/agentsFiles; system prompt = XTS prompt (PRD §12.1, acceptance 2/3/4)
- src/cli.mjs wires all four modes:
  - `xts` interactive: TUI + streaming + guarded bash + prompt history + conversation persistence
  - `xts "question"` one-shot: print answer, exit (PRD §20.2)
  - `command | xts ["question"]`: stdin evidence + answer, exit (PRD §20.3)
  - `xts run "command"`: gate -> execute -> result to model for interpretation -> display (PRD §20.4)
- Conversation persistence: interactive sessions continue previous turns; `SessionManager` handles message history save (PRD §17.2); one-shot uses in-memory or named session
- Model unavailable at session start -> selector (from task 2) or clear error in non-TTY
- All events wired: message streaming to TUI/stdout, tool execution rows, errors returned to model with exact shell evidence (PRD §21)

## SCOPE

- packages/xts/src/runtime.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/src/cli.mjs (extend)
- packages/xts/src/main.ts-style entry (if needed)
- test/runtime.test.mjs, test/cli.test.mjs (integration tests with stubbed SDK where needed)

## NON_GOALS

- No RPC mode, no server mode, no extensions, no skills, no MCP wiring
- No multi-session tree UI
- No automatic model fallback

## CONSTRAINTS

- Lazy imports: the SDK (pi-coding-agent) imported only when a model-requiring mode runs, keeping `xts --help` and `xts shellhook` instant
- ResourceLoader: implement minimal explicit loader returning empty collections (pattern: examples/sdk/12-full-control.ts resourceLoader object) — do NOT call DefaultResourceLoader discovery
- SessionManager: default SessionManager.create(cwd) for interactive (conversation history); one-shot may use SessionManager.inMemory(cwd)
- Bash tool: createBashTool with operations wrapping the safety gate (classify -> approve -> exec) so every model bash call is gated; `xts run` calls the same gate directly
- Thinking level: off for fast answers (configurable later); auto-retry off to keep behavior deterministic
- Errors: model/tool failures surface exact evidence; never report success on failure
- All user-facing messages concise; exit codes: 0 success, 1 errors, 2 usage

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Integration test (stubbed SDK or live if auth available): one-shot returns answer text; pipe mode includes stdin evidence in prompt
- [ ] Closed-surface assertion test: resourceLoader.getExtensions()/getSkills()/getPrompts()/getThemes()/getAgentsFiles() all empty; system prompt is the XTS prompt
- [ ] Interactive smoke: start `xts` in a pty, send prompt, receive streamed answer, conversation persists to session file
- [ ] `xts run` safe command executes; dangerous command gated
- [ ] Perf: cold `xts --help` <300ms; `xts "q"` startup (model load + context) measured and reported
- [ ] node --test green

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: tasks 1-6 modules
- Installed deps: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.84.2 (createAgentSession, ModelRuntime, SessionManager, SettingsManager, createBashTool), @earendil-works/pi-tui@0.84.2
- Stdlib: node:child_process (spawn for run mode), node:readline (one-shot approval fallback)
- New dep candidate: none
- Roll it: yes — final integration task

## OUTPUT

runtime.mjs + cli.mjs wiring, integration test output, closed-surface evidence, interactive smoke notes, perf measurements, sample session file path.
close_reason: Integration complete and independently verified through remediation children: .7.1 pipe/stdin PASS (both pipe forms read to EOF, hard caps, split UTF-8), .7.2 TUI/Pi runtime PASS (authoritative Model, single ModelRuntime, append-only transcript, visible errors, hydration, lifecycle cleanup), .7.3 safety/privacy PASS (30-probe classifier set, deny-before-exec sentinel, pre-persistence redaction, private modes, live Zsh capture). Closed surface and bash-only tool asserted at runtime. Full suite 129/129 in isolated run. Perf measurement and 27-criteria acceptance evidence owned by xtrm-nka.8, in progress.

title: Safety gate — dangerous-command classifier + approval flow
description:
## PROBLEM

PRD §14: the bash tool must sit behind a deterministic, small safety gate. Dangerous commands (recursive destructive deletes, formatting, raw disk writes, privileged destructive ops, dangerous permission changes, destructive git ops, configured high-risk patterns) require explicit user approval before execution. Denied commands must not execute.

## SUCCESS

- src/safety/classify.mjs: command classifier returning { safe: true } or { safe: false, reason, pattern } for dangerous commands; adopts the minimal concept from pi-guardrails permission-gate (structural matchers for rm -rf, shred, sudo/doas/pkexec, dd of=, mkfs/wipefs/blkdiscard/fdisk/parted, chmod -R 777, chown -R, docker/podman dangerous flags) — implemented locally, not by loading the Guardrails package (PRD §14.1)
- src/safety/approve.mjs: approval flow — interactive overlay/prompt (Enter approve once, Esc cancel) shown in the TUI; in one-shot (non-TTY) mode, approval prompts on stdin with clear y/n; default is deny (PRD §14.2)
- Gate is integrated with the bash tool execution path so EVERY bash call goes through it: safe -> execute; dangerous -> approval -> execute or block; blocked -> model receives a clear "command denied" result, conversation continues (PRD §21)
- `xts run "command"` uses the same gate (PRD §7.4): classify first, approve if dangerous, execute, pass result to model for interpretation when needed
- Cancelled/denied commands are not executed (PRD §21)

## SCOPE

- packages/xts/src/safety/classify.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/src/safety/approve.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/src/runtime.mjs (integrate gate into bash tool via createBashTool operations/spawnHook or tool wrapper; owned by task 7 wiring — this task provides classify+approve and a `gateCommand(command, ctx)` function)
- packages/xts/src/cli.mjs (wire `xts run`)

## NON_GOALS

- No "always allow"/session-allow/policy editor/custom rule UI (PRD §14.2)
- No file-access policies (Guardrails policies/path-access are out of scope)
- No loading the full @aliou/pi-guardrails package at runtime

## CONSTRAINTS

- Classifier is deterministic pure logic (no I/O); unit-testable
- Structural matching: parse command words (simple tokenizer adequate for v1; full AST not required) and match command+flags; also support configured extra patterns from XTS config optional array
- Default deny on approval timeout/EOF; one-shot mode must never execute a dangerous command without explicit user yes
- Gate must run BEFORE any execution; wrap the bash tool so the gate sees every command (including chained `&&`/`|` segments — classify the whole string, conservative)
- Redaction: do not log full command payloads in gate failure logs

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests: each dangerous pattern family classified dangerous with reason; benign variants (rm file, git pull, ls, npm test) classified safe; false-positive guards (rm -rf denied, rm -f file allowed, mkdir -p allowed)
- [ ] Integration: `xts run "rm -rf /tmp/x"` prompts, deny -> not executed (evidence: temp dir still exists)
- [ ] Integration: `xts run "echo hi"` executes without approval
- [ ] Approved dangerous command executes
- [ ] node --test green

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: none
- Installed deps: none new at runtime (classifier implemented locally, adapted from @aliou/pi-guardrails@0.16.1 src/core/commands/dangerous.ts patterns — read-only reference)
- Stdlib: none
- New dep candidate: none — local implementation keeps XTS small and dependency-free
- Roll it: yes

## OUTPUT

classify.mjs + approve.mjs + tests, pattern coverage list, integration evidence for the three `xts run` scenarios above.
close_reason: Safety gate done: safety/classify.mjs (deterministic, guardrails-parity + git destructive ops, extraPatterns), safety/approve.mjs (runGate, stdin fallback, default deny), run.mjs (executeGuarded). cli run wired. Manual evidence: echo hi execs; rm -rf denied not executed. 66/66 green.

title: TUI — conversation view, input, model selector overlay, approval overlay
description:

Interactive mode wiring is task 7.

title: Stdin pipe mode + bounded truncation + system prompt assembly
description:
## PROBLEM

PRD §7.3/§11: `command | xts` and `command | xts "question"` must treat stdin as first-class evidence with bounded input and an explicit truncation notice. PRD §15: the system prompt must be intentionally small. Both feed the same prompt builder.

## SUCCESS

- src/stdin.mjs: reads stdin asynchronously; bounds input — max bytes (e.g. 64KB) and max lines (e.g. 2000); when truncated, records truncation metadata (original bytes/lines, what was kept) — silent truncation never happens (PRD §11.1)
- src/prompt.mjs: builds the small XTS system prompt (PRD §15 conceptual content, tuned) + per-run user message envelope that includes: user instruction (if any), ShellContext (cwd, shell, lastExitCode, recentCommands from task 3), stdin evidence block (with visible "stdin truncated" notice when applicable), and the guarded-execution context marker
- The envelope renders into the first user message sent to the model; system prompt stays fixed and small
- Prompt builder is pure (no I/O) and unit-testable

## SCOPE

- packages/xts/src/stdin.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/src/prompt.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/src/context.mjs (consume; owned by task 3)
- test/stdin.test.mjs, test/prompt.test.mjs (new)

## NON_GOALS

- No streaming stdin processing; no partial-read heuristics
- No transcript capture

## CONSTRAINTS

- Truncation policy constants exported: MAX_STDIN_BYTES=65536, MAX_STDIN_LINES=2000; strategy: keep head, then head-of-tail marker "[... stdin truncated: X of Y bytes (Z lines) ...]" visible to model and user
- System prompt token budget: keep under ~200 tokens; measured via prompt.mjs test asserting approximate length
- ShellContext rendered compactly (one block, no prose) so tokens stay small
- Do not emit secrets: stdin content is user-provided evidence (allowed), but the envelope must not auto-include env vars or credentials

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests: small stdin passes through whole; huge stdin truncated with visible notice; truncation metadata exact; prompt envelope contains cwd/exit code/recent commands/notice
- [ ] System prompt size assert (< 200 tokens by heuristic char count)
- [ ] node --test green

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: context.mjs (task 3), config.mjs (task 1)
- Installed deps: none new
- Stdlib: node:stream, node:buffer
- New dep candidate: none
- Roll it: yes

## OUTPUT

stdin.mjs + prompt.mjs + tests, sample built prompt (with and without stdin/truncation), token-size measurement.
close_reason: Stdin+prompt done: src/stdin.mjs (bounded read, explicit truncation notice, mid-line finish rules, 8 tests), src/prompt.mjs (SYSTEM_PROMPT ~50 tokens, buildUserMessage envelope, estimateTokens). cli one-shot wired with non-blocking pipe detection (maybeReadStdin). 91/91 tests green.

title: Shell context — silent shell integration, cwd/lastExitCode/recent commands
description:
## PROBLEM

PRD §9/§10: standard invocations must automatically receive bounded shell context (cwd, shell identity, last exit code, last 10 commands) via a silent shell integration. The integration must print nothing after commands and must not capture stdout/stderr/transcripts.

## SUCCESS

- src/history/shell.mjs: reads bounded shell context — cwd, shell identity, last exit code, last N=10 commands — from a compact state file written by a silent shell hook
- src/history/hook.sh: bash hook fragment + src/history/hook.zsh (or one generator with both) that writes the state file after each command; emits zero stdout/stderr
- `xts shellhook` (dev command) prints the hook snippet for the current shell and instructions (source it in ~/.bashrc / ~/.zshrc); supports bash and zsh (PRD §10.2)
- Context unavailable (no hook installed): XTS still works with cwd + stdin + manual question; recent-shell context clearly omitted (PRD §21)
- Sensitive command filtering: commands containing obvious secret forms (token=, password=, api[_-]?key=, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY blocks, `key=...` assignment with long value) are redacted from the recent-command list (PRD §25 open item — implement deterministically and conservatively)

## SCOPE

- packages/xts/src/history/shell.mjs (new: state read + redaction)
- packages/xts/src/history/hook.bash / hook.zsh (new)
- packages/xts/src/cli.mjs (wire `xts shellhook` + context assembly)
- packages/xts/src/context.mjs (new: assemble ShellContext envelope for the model prompt)

## NON_GOALS

- No transcript capture, no environment-variable capture, no scrollback capture (PRD §9.3, §22)
- No fish/PowerShell hooks (PRD §26)
- No auto-install of hooks into user shell config

## CONSTRAINTS

- Hook writes state to a fixed path: $XDG_STATE_HOME/xts/state.json or ~/.local/state/xts/state.json; format: { cwd, shell, lastExitCode, recentCommands: [...] } (last 10)
- Hook must be silent: no echo, no ANSI output, no errors visible; failures must not affect the shell
- Redaction: deterministic conservative patterns only (see SUCCESS); redacted entries replaced with "[redacted]"
- ShellContext envelope rendered into the model prompt (prompt.mjs task 5 consumes it); this task provides the data module only
- Do not touch model/prompt/safety/UI modules

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests: redaction patterns (secret forms redacted, normal commands intact), bounded N=10, corrupt/missing state -> graceful empty context
- [ ] Manual smoke: install hook in bash, run commands, verify state file content and zero hook output
- [ ] zsh hook syntax check (zsh -n if available)
- [ ] `xts shellhook` prints snippet and instructions
- [ ] node --test green

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: none beyond task 1 config
- Installed deps: none new (hook is pure shell; state read uses node:fs)
- Stdlib: node:fs, node:os
- New dep candidate: none
- Roll it: yes

## OUTPUT

shell.mjs + hooks + context.mjs, test evidence, sample state file, redaction test output, shellhook output sample.
close_reason: Shell context done: history/shell.mjs (state read, redaction, loadShellContext, formatShellContext), hook.bash + hook.zsh (silent, atomic, no jq), context.mjs re-export, cli shellhook wired. 12 shell tests; bash+zsh smokes show zero hook output and redaction works. 66/66 green.

title: Model resolution — Pi ModelRuntime inventory + xts model selector + persistence
description:
## PROBLEM

PRD §8 requires explicit, persisted model selection sourced from Pi's model inventory — never Pi's default, never silent substitution. First launch must show a selector of available (authenticated) models; `xts model` reopens it; the selected provider/model pair persists to ~/.config/xtrm/xts.json.

## SUCCESS

- src/model.mjs: `resolveModel(runtime, config)` returns the persisted model if available; `listAvailable(runtime)` returns models from ModelRuntime.getAvailable() grouped by provider; `pickModel` runs the selector
- Model inventory authority is Pi's ModelRuntime (built-ins + models.json + auth); XTS stores only the preference (PRD §8.2)
- `xts model` opens a keyboard-navigable model selector (up/down, enter confirm, esc cancel) and persists selection; `xts model --json` (dev flag) prints the inventory for tests
- First launch with no persisted model opens the selector; if selection cancelled -> exit 1 with clear message
- Selected model unavailable (auth missing/removed): `xts` shows message + reopens selector; never auto-falls-back (PRD §8.4, §21)
- Non-interactive fallback: when stdin is not a TTY and no model persisted, error clearly (no selector possible)

## SCOPE

- packages/xts/src/model.mjs (new)
- packages/xts/src/config.mjs (extend read/write if needed)
- packages/xts/src/ui/model-selector.mjs (new, minimal TUI selector using pi-tui)
- packages/xts/src/cli.mjs (wire `xts model` and first-launch selector)

## NON_GOALS

- No model auto-cycle/fallback (PRD §8.4)
- No OAuth login UI (auth stays Pi-owned; error message tells user to run `pi` to authenticate)
- No settings UI

## CONSTRAINTS

- ModelRuntime.create() with default authPath/modelsPath (~/.pi/agent) so Pi auth + models.json are authoritative; allowModelNetwork: false, refreshOnCreate: false (startup must stay fast — snapshot + lazy refresh only)
- Persist exactly { model: { provider, id } } in ~/.config/xtrm/xts.json (config.mjs owns file I/O)
- If runtime.getAvailable() is empty: error message instructs configuring auth through Pi (`pi`) — no second auth system
- Selector uses pi-tui (ProcessTerminal + Input/SelectList-style list or minimal custom component); keyboard: ↑↓ select, Enter confirm, Esc cancel
- Must NOT silently choose a different model at session start

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xts model --json` prints inventory JSON from ModelRuntime (grep test)
- [ ] Config write/read round trip of selected model
- [ ] First-launch path (no config) yields selector; cancel -> exit 1 with message
- [ ] Missing/unavailable model -> clear error, no fallback substitution (unit test with stub runtime)
- [ ] node --test green for model module tests

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: config.mjs from task 1; pi-tui selector pattern: pi-coding-agent dist/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.d.ts (read-only reference)
- Installed deps: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (ModelRuntime), @earendil-works/pi-tui (ProcessTerminal, Container, Text, Input)
- Stdlib: node:fs/promises
- New dep candidate: none — reuse Pi inventory
- Roll it: yes

## OUTPUT

model.mjs + selector implementation, test output, `xts model --json` sample, config file sample, evidence that unavailable model does not auto-fallback.
close_reason: Model resolution done: model.mjs (listAvailable/resolveModel/requireAvailableModels/inventoryToJson/resolveOrSelectModel), ui/model-selector.mjs (pi-tui SelectList selector, pty-verified), cli wired (model + model --json). 16 model tests, 66/66 suite green. Persisted model: commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash.

title: XTS v1 — minimal shell assistant on Pi SDK + pi-tui
description:
## PROBLEM

Normal coding agents (Pi/XTRM) carry far more runtime and cognitive machinery than a small terminal problem requires: skills, extensions, Beads, specialists, MCP, GitNexus, repository workflows. A user who just wants "why did that pull fail?" or "what is listening on 8080?" should not pay that startup and context cost. XTS must be a separate, closed-runtime terminal assistant that starts fast, carries bounded shell context automatically, exposes exactly one operational tool (bash) behind a deterministic safety gate, and stays materially smaller than a normal Pi session. PRD: packages/xts/xts-prd-0.1.0.md.

## SUCCESS

An `xts` binary in packages/xts that satisfies all 27 PRD acceptance criteria (PRD §24): standalone startup with no Pi/XTRM resource discovery; explicit persisted model selection from Pi's ModelRuntime inventory; bounded shell context (cwd, last exit code, last 10 commands); one-shot `xts "question"`; stdin pipe mode with explicit bounded truncation; `xts run` through the deterministic dangerous-command gate; interactive conversation with streaming, prompt history, and persisted conversation history; compact TUI built on @earendil-works/pi-tui; startup overhead substantially below model latency.

## SCOPE

- packages/xts/ — new package (package.json, src/, test/, README.md, shell hook installer)
- PRD contract: packages/xts/xts-prd-0.1.0.md (read-only reference)
- Read-only dependencies (do NOT modify): @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.84.2 (global SDK), @earendil-works/pi-tui@0.84.2, @aliou/pi-guardrails@0.16.1 (classifier reference)

## NON_GOALS

- No skills, Specialists, Beads, MCP, GitNexus, LSP, repository indexing, subagents, RLM, memory promotion, extension discovery, file-editing tools (PRD §5)
- No automatic model switching/fallback; no automatic invocation after shell failures
- No "always allow" / session-allow / policy editor / custom rule UI for the safety gate (PRD §14.2)
- No full terminal transcript capture (PRD §9.3)
- No fish/PowerShell support, no searchable global history, no model-switch shortcut (PRD §26)
- Do NOT modify the Pi SDK, pi-tui, or pi-guardrails packages

## CONSTRAINTS

- Plain ESM JavaScript (.mjs) following packages/xtprompt convention; no build step, no TypeScript compile
- node >= 24; tests via `node --test` (see test/README.md)
- Startup must not initialize: skills, extensions, MCP, Beads subprocesses, GitNexus, AGENTS scanning, package inventory scanning, LSP, Python kernels (PRD §18)
- Tool surface = bash only (PRD §13); guard via createAgentSession({ tools: ["bash"], ... }) with custom bash tool (createBashTool with operations/spawnHook)
- Model selection explicit; persist { provider, id } in ~/.config/xtrm/xts.json; never silently substitute (PRD §8)
- Shell integration must be silent (no post-command hints) (PRD §10)
- Config location: ~/.config/xtrm/xts.json (small file)
- Conversation persistence via Pi SessionManager (default ~/.pi/agent/sessions or per-PRD evaluation); PRD §17
- Logging/telemetry contract: XTS may log to stderr (one-shot) or a debug env flag XTS_DEBUG=1; log lines: timestamp, level, component, event, duration_ms, redacted context. Never log credentials or command output payloads.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] All 27 PRD §24 acceptance criteria verified with concrete evidence
- [ ] `node --test` suite green in packages/xts
- [ ] Startup timing measured: cold process startup and time-to-TUI recorded in test/perf notes
- [ ] Smoke run: `xts model` lists inventory, one-shot `echo hi | xts "say hi"` style checks work against authenticated models
- [ ] Shell integration silent (no stdout pollution after a command)
- [ ] Safety gate: dangerous command requires approval, denied commands not executed
- [ ] No XTS startup path initializes skills/extensions/MCP/Beads (verified by code inspection + perf)
- [ ] Per-task OUTPUT sections populated in bead close reasons

## OUTPUT

Orchestrator reports: per-child handoff summary referencing each bead's OUTPUT, integration evidence (smoke + tests), performance measurements, residual risks (open questions from PRD §25).

## REFERENCES

- PRD: packages/xts/xts-prd-0.1.0.md
- SDK docs: /home/dawid/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/sdk.md
- TUI docs: .../pi-tui/dist/index.d.ts (Container/Input/Markdown/Box/VStack/SelectList)
- Classifier reference: .../pi-guardrails/extensions/permission-gate/rules.ts + src/core/commands/dangerous.ts
- Convention reference: packages/xtprompt/src/*.mjs

Per-child outcomes: .1 scaffold, .2 model resolution (explicit persisted selection from Pi inventory, no fallback), .3 silent bash/zsh shell context with pre-persistence redaction, .4 bounded stdin + small prompt, .5 safety gate (deny-default), .6 pi-tui conversation UI, .7 runtime/CLI wiring closed via verified children .7.1 pipe/stdin PASS, .7.2 TUI/Pi runtime PASS, .7.3 classifier/privacy PASS; .8 acceptance audit: 27/27 PRD §24 criteria evidenced in test/acceptance.md; .8.1 suite-crash root-caused as coordinator-harness interaction (no product defect); .9 independent audit drove 4 release-blocker fixes (pipe dispatch, first-launch model resolution, transcript retention, gate bypasses). Integration evidence: full suite 131/131 isolated; e2e 14/14 incl. PTY retained-answer and two-session persistence; perf cold ~60ms / TUI ~0.9s / Enter-to-answer 1.6-2.0s incl. model latency — init overhead far below model latency (PRD §18, criterion 26). title: chain-runtime: emit sre-triage-runs bundle at terminal state (satisfied OR escalated)
description:
## PROBLEM

The archive shape lives in mercury/infra (epic infra-223r, local bead infra-223r.5): every terminal sre-triage chain run must write a durable per-run bundle into the target repo at `services/sre-triage-runs/<UTC>_<chain_id_short>/`. Nothing in this chain runtime emits bundles today — the archive stays empty except for the seeded example in mercury/infra (.3). The WRITER must live here (experiments/agentsession-sre-chain-vertical-slice/src/chain), not in mercury/infra.

## SUCCESS

A small pure function (in a new src/chain/finalize.ts, or in scheduler.ts) called from the terminal-state handler emits a bundle for BOTH terminal states (satisfied AND escalated) at exactly:

    <target-repo>/.xtrm/skills/infra/service-knowledge/services/sre-triage-runs/<UTC>_<chain_id_short>/

with the deterministic file list:

- chain-report.v1.json (schema key 'schema': 'chain-report.v1' at top level; includes next_actions[] array)
- report.md (coordinator hand-written narrative: incident brief, findings, gotchas, fixes, workarounds, deferred, next-actions — written by the coordinator as its coordinator.decision evidence body, materialized by this writer)
- gotchas.jsonl (one JSON object per line: {"kind":..., "resource":..., "symptom":..., "evidence_ref":..., "fix_applied":..., "worked":true|false, "prior_run_refs":[]})
- evidence/*.json (the run's evidence entries from evidence/index.jsonl, expanded one file each)
- forensics.jsonl (copy of forensics/events.jsonl)
- messages.jsonl (copy of channels/messages.jsonl)

Plus ONE structured event in the run's forensics/events.jsonl:

    sre-triage.bundle.written  fields: {chain_id, chain_run_id, bundle_path, terminal_state, files_written[], bytes_written, elapsed_ms}

## SCOPE

- src/chain/finalize.ts (new) or scheduler.ts — the terminal-state handler hook.
- Reuse src/chain/store.ts paths() for the run's evidence/forensics/messages sources.

## NON_GOALS

- No new package. Writer is a small pure function.
- Failure to write the bundle is a fact.warning (NOT fatal) — a write failure must not sink an otherwise-successful chain.
- Do NOT change the bundle shape declared in mercury/infra .3/.4 — this repo materializes it.
- No changes to mercury/infra from this issue.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Writer: small pure function in finalize.ts (or scheduler.ts) called from the terminal-state handler; no new package.
- Bundle path template: services/sre-triage-runs/<UTC>_<chain_id_short>/ (UTC ISO compact, e.g. 20260819T015344Z).
- Redaction: no raw secrets, no full env dumps, no PII in report.md or gotchas.jsonl.
- The sre-triage.bundle.written event fields: {chain_id, chain_run_id, bundle_path, terminal_state, files_written, bytes_written, elapsed_ms}.
- Sequencing: this issue references the two existing findings filed earlier — xtrm-pq1.1 (coordinator contract adherence: coordinator must call evidence_publish(kind=coordinator.decision)) and xtrm-pq1.2 (bridge/custom-provider resolution: model not found for commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash). The bundle writer depends on both landing: pq1.1 fixes coordinator-entry satisfaction (so a run reaches terminal state), pq1.2 fixes specialist dispatch on custom providers.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] One live chain run emits a bundle at the exact path template with all six required files.
- [ ] Bundle passes the shape check from mercury/infra infra-223r.3 (chain-report.v1.json schema key, gotchas.jsonl line shape, report.md headings).
- [ ] sre-triage.bundle.written event present in that run's forensics/events.jsonl (grep passes).
- [ ] Both terminal states covered: satisfied run AND escalated run each emit.
- [ ] Write failure does not crash the chain (fact.warning only).

## OUTPUT

- Path of the first live-emitted bundle under services/sre-triage-runs/.
- One grep line from that run's forensics showing sre-triage.bundle.written.
- Confirmation of both terminal states covered.

## LIBRARIES

N/A — small pure TS function in the existing experiment package.

## NOTES

Filed from mercury/infra epic infra-223r (local tracking bead infra-223r.5). The mercury/infra side owns the SHAPE (docs in services/sre-triage-runs/SKILL.md + INDEXING-DECISION.md); this issue owns the WRITER. Cross-repo sequencing: do NOT merge before xtrm-pq1.1 + xtrm-pq1.2 are addressed (they fix coordinator-entry satisfaction + custom-provider dispatch that a real chain needs to reach terminal state).

title: CLI robustness and exit-code polish (F4-F7)
description:
# PROBLEM

Minor but user-visible defects in error paths. (F4) Ctrl-C at the clarification prompt exits 1 with "clarification input failed." instead of signaling an interrupt (empirically confirmed via PTY: exit 1); ask() in src/cli.mjs:7-14 has no SIGINT handling. (F5) An explicit --model for an existing but unauthenticated provider passes selectModel (src/app.mjs:208-213; resolveCliModel deliberately resolves unauthenticated models) and fails later at completion with exit 1 and the F1 misdiagnosis, while README classifies invalid model selection as exit 2. (F6) SettingsManager.create/getDefaultProvider/getDefaultModel at src/app.mjs:215-217 are unguarded; a throw escapes selectModel as an unhandled rejection crash; resolveCliModel's warning (e.g. "Using custom model id") is silently dropped at :212. (F7) No EPIPE handling: `xtprompt ... | head -0` crashes with an uncaught error event on process.stdout.

# SUCCESS

Ctrl-C at the clarification prompt exits 130 with an honest message (or a documented deliberate alternative). An unauthenticated explicit --model exits 2 with a clear "not authenticated" diagnostic before any completion call. A settings-read failure degrades to "no default configured" instead of crashing. resolveCliModel warnings reach stderr. Closed-pipe output exits cleanly without a stack trace.

# SCOPE

src/cli.mjs (ask at :7-14, main at :52-54), src/app.mjs (selectModel at :208-233, stdout/stderr write paths at :134-141), test/app.test.mjs, test/pty.test.mjs (a SIGINT-at-clarification case if feasible with the script harness).

# NON_GOALS

- No change to interactive-mode SIGINT semantics during in-flight model calls (that is F15, tracked separately in T7).
- No change to the F1 retry logic (must be landed first; this task builds on its harness).

# CONSTRAINTS

- F5's fix (auth check after resolveCliModel) must run after F1's harness change is in place (T1 blocks this task) because both reshape app.test.mjs's model-failure mocks.
- Diagnostics stay secret-safe and never echo the model body or prompt.
- Exit codes stay within the documented 0/1/2/130 taxonomy.

# VALIDATION

- [ ] PTY test: Ctrl-C at "What exact outcome..." exits 130 with an interrupt message (or the accepted alternative is recorded in README and tested).
- [ ] Test: --model with unauthenticated provider -> exit 2, stderr mentions not authenticated, zero completion calls.
- [ ] Test: settingsManager.getDefaultProvider throws -> runCli still resolves models via getAvailable, no crash.
- [ ] Test: resolveCliModel returns a warning -> warning appears on stderr.
- [ ] Test: stdout write error (closed pipe) -> clean exit, no uncaught exception.
- [ ] Full suite + coverage green.

# OUTPUT

Changed files, per-defect test evidence, exit-code table after the change, residual risk (EPIPE behavior on the real CLI pipe under different shells).

(EOF/input error stays 1); unauthenticated explicit --model -> exit 2 before any completion call; SettingsManager failures degrade with warning; resolveCliModel warning to stderr; EPIPE -> quiet exit 0. title: Prompt-parsing edge-case hardening (F9-F13)
description:
# PROBLEM

Minor edge cases in parsing and filtering. (F9) normalizeContext slices UTF-16 code units (src/prompt.mjs:85-87), so 480 emoji/CJK code points become 240 "characters" and a boundary can split a surrogate pair into a lone surrogate (encoded as U+FFFD); the 480-char unit is undocumented. (F10) The control-byte filter range in isActionableRewrite (src/app.mjs:372) includes CR (0x0d), so a model response with CRLF line endings is rejected and can fail the whole run after one retry. (F11) isClarificationOnly (src/prompt.mjs:187-192) requires a leading interrogative word, so "Need more details?" passes and can be emitted as the final prompt. (F12) extractAssistantText (src/prompt.mjs:210-216) throws TypeError when message.content is a plain string instead of a parts array (empirically confirmed). (F13) parseSentinel (src/prompt.mjs:180-185) pairs first OPEN with last CLOSE, so multi-block output like <xtprompt>a</xtprompt> and <xtprompt>b</xtprompt> yields garbled content "a</xtprompt> and <xtprompt>b" that passes the actionable check and reaches stdout.

# SUCCESS

All five edge cases are handled: the 480-cap is defined and implemented over code points (documented unit); CRLF model output is not falsely rejected; unprefixed clarification questions are caught or the detection contract is documented; extractAssistantText handles both string and parts-array content; multi-block sentinel output is rejected as malformed (retried) rather than garbled. Each case has a regression test.

# SCOPE

src/prompt.mjs (normalizeContext :85-87, isClarificationOnly :187-192, extractAssistantText :210-216, parseSentinel :180-185), src/app.mjs (isActionableRewrite :369-373), test/prompt.test.mjs, test/app.test.mjs, README.md (document the 480-char unit).

# NON_GOALS

- No change to which control bytes are allowed beyond excluding CR (TAB/LF stay allowed, C0-minus-TAB/LF/DEL/C1 stay rejected).
- No clipboard payload-size guard (that is F14, tracked in T7).

# CONSTRAINTS

- parseSentinel change must keep the existing valid single-block behavior byte-for-byte.
- The CR exemption must not re-open an injection vector; verify CR alone cannot form an OSC/CSI sequence (it cannot: sequences start with ESC).
- isClarificationOnly broadening must not cause actionable question-phrased prompts to be retried excessively; keep the retry-once cap.
- This task touches app.mjs regions adjacent to T1's edits; land after T1 (T1 blocks this task).

# VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests: normalizeContext with a 480+ astral-char string -> no lone surrogate, length documented and asserted; isClarificationOnly("Need more details?") -> true (or contract documented); extractAssistantText({content:"plain"}) -> "plain" without throwing; parseSentinel multi-block -> undefined (malformed).
- [ ] app-level test: a CRLF-wrapped <xtprompt> response is accepted on the first attempt (no retry).
- [ ] Existing control-byte tests (app.test.mjs:192-205) stay green.
- [ ] Full suite + coverage green.

# OUTPUT

Changed files, per-case before/after behavior, test evidence, the documented 480-char unit in README, residual risk (real providers' CRLF and string-content behavior still unverified without live calls).
close_reason: F9-F13 fixed: 480-cap over code points (Array.from, no lone surrogate); CR allowed in control-byte gate (CRLF passes); isClarificationOnly catches unprefixed '?' sentences; extractAssistantText handles string content; parseSentinel rejects multi-block, single-block byte-identical. Regression tests each; README 480 'characters (code points)'. 60 tests green.

title: Add interactive prompt refinement loop and :accept
description:
## PROBLEM

A one-shot rewrite cannot be incrementally refined. Re-running the command loses the accepted prompt state and gives the user no structured way to accept, undo, or quit.

## SUCCESS

`xtprompt --interactive "draft"` creates an initial rewrite, then accepts free-text refinement instructions until the user runs a command. `:accept` copies the current prompt and exits, `:show` reprints it, `:undo` restores the previous valid revision, `:help` lists commands, and `:quit`/EOF exits without copying.

## SCOPE

Interactive orchestration in `packages/xtprompt/src/app.mjs` and `src/cli.mjs`, refinement request policy in `src/prompt.mjs`, CLI help/README, and integration tests. Reuse the clipboard primitive from the sibling task.

## NON_GOALS

- No Pi `AgentSession`, tools, automatic code inspection, session files, resume command, or full conversation transcript.
- No full-screen TUI, syntax highlighting, multiline editor, named sessions, or branching history.
- No unbounded history; keep current and previous valid prompt only.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Require a TTY for interactive mode.
- Treat non-command input as a refinement instruction, not as a new source prompt or general chat.
- Send only current prompt, latest refinement instruction, intent, and bounded advisory context to `completeSimple()`.
- A failed or clarification-only rewrite must preserve the current prompt and keep the loop usable.
- `:accept` must use the clipboard task's injected transport and close readline resources deterministically.
- User-visible state changes and failures go to stderr; deliberate prompt display remains readable and secret-safe. Do not persist prompts or model responses.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Integration tests cover initial rewrite, two refinements, `:show`, `:undo`, `:help`, `:accept`, `:quit`, EOF, and unsupported commands.
- [ ] Failure tests prove model/copy errors preserve the last valid prompt and leave no hanging readline handle.
- [ ] Existing one-shot positional/stdin/JSON behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] PTY smoke runs a scripted refinement followed by `:accept` and verifies clean exit plus OSC 52 emission.
- [ ] Live authenticated smoke verifies a two-turn refinement produces an actionable accepted prompt.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** `completeRewrite`, prompt sentinel validation, model selection, and `node:readline/promises` already used by `src/cli.mjs`.
- **Installed deps:** existing Pi SDK `ModelRuntime.completeSimple()` remains the model boundary.
- **Stdlib:** `node:readline/promises` provides the line-oriented loop and deterministic close.
- **New dep candidate:** none; a TUI framework is unnecessary for this command loop.
- **Roll it:** yes, as a small in-memory state loop over existing functions.

## OUTPUT

Hand back the command grammar, state-transition behavior, transcript samples, changed files, tests, live smoke evidence, and explicit non-agent limitations.
notes:
SCRUTINY: medium. Depends on verified xtrm-s6s.1 clipboard primitive. Use TDD, no AgentSession, no git operations.
Implemented by delegated subagent and independently verified. Added --interactive/-i, current+previous state loop, refinement requests, :show/:undo/:help/:accept/:quit, EOF and failure recovery, docs and integration tests. Parent reran tests, coverage, syntax, and help successfully.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in-memory interactive refinement with accept/copy, undo, show, help, quit, and failure recovery.

title: Add OSC 52 clipboard output and --copy
description:
## PROBLEM

One-shot `xtprompt` output must be selected and copied manually. On this SSH-oriented workflow, GUI clipboard libraries cannot reliably reach the operator's local clipboard.

## SUCCESS

`xtprompt --copy "draft"` preserves normal prompt output and also sends the rewritten prompt through OSC 52. Tmux sessions receive the required passthrough wrapper. Copy failures produce concise stderr diagnostics and never replace a successful prompt with control data on stdout.

## SCOPE

`packages/xtprompt/src/clipboard.mjs` (new), argument/output wiring in `packages/xtprompt/src/app.mjs`, help and README text, and focused tests.

## NON_GOALS

- No clipboard read support.
- No `clipboardy`, `xclip`, `wl-copy`, `pbcopy`, or desktop-session discovery.
- No automatic copying unless `--copy` is explicitly selected or `:accept` is used by the later interactive task.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Encode prompt bytes as Base64 and emit OSC 52 only to an injected terminal/control stream, never ordinary stdout.
- Support plain terminal and tmux passthrough forms.
- Reject copy when no TTY/control stream is available instead of silently claiming success.
- Diagnostics may state outcome and transport only; do not echo the prompt.
- Telemetry is limited to exit code and concise stderr because this local CLI has no persistent logging subsystem.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests assert exact plain and tmux OSC 52 sequences for Unicode input.

## LIBRARIES

- **Installed deps:** none applicable; Pi SDK does not provide clipboard transport.
- **Stdlib:** `Buffer.from(text).toString("base64")` and writable streams cover OSC 52.
- **New dep candidate:** none; desktop clipboard packages do not solve remote SSH reliably.
- **Roll it:** yes, as a small terminal protocol encoder with no external dependency.

title: PR5a: eval corpus + telemetry dashboards + alert-to-service routing
description:
## PROBLEM

PR0-4 ship package + verifier + gate + index + dispatch integration. Without measurement, we cannot answer: does the verifier catch what it should? Is retrieval precision high enough? What's the stale-claim escape rate? Are agents actually consuming bundles?

Research §3.9 mandates a labeled eval corpus (80-150 cases from real closed issues / merged PRs / real alerts / incidents / drift history / diagnostic tasks) with a specific metric set. Research §3.7 requires retrieval telemetry (retrieval_events table) for ignored-activation rate, citation utilization rate, stale-claim escape rate. PR3 declared the table; this PR populates it with hooks and dashboards.

**Ponytail split**: canary policy for future auto-merge is a decision doc, not code. Split into PR5b — unblocks separately when operator ratifies thresholds. This PR (PR5a) is shovel-ready measurement + alert-to-service surface.

## SUCCESS

- Labeled eval corpus at ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/eval/corpus/ with 80-150 cases across: closed bd issues (bug + feature), merged PRs with operational changes, real Prometheus alerts (from mercury-infra history), incident reports, drift history, diagnostic tasks, past questions that produced wrong commands or claims.
- Each case labeled per §3.9: query_or_task, touched_paths, expected_services, required_evidence, forbidden_evidence, expected_probes, cross_repo_required, outcome.
- Eval harness runs the corpus against the shipped system and emits the 12 metrics from §3.9.
- Retrieval telemetry hooks emit to retrieval_events (PR3 table) on every knowledge_search/_get/_evidence_for_files call + on every activator invocation.
- Weekly report at .beads/eval-reports/YYYY-WW.md (raw values, week-over-week delta, threshold status green/yellow/red, corpus expansion suggestions).
- Alert-to-service routing tool (new small MCP wrapper): incident_routing takes an Alertmanager-shaped payload → knowledge_search → returns top-K service + runbook probes → evidence bundle. Advisory only.
- Post-merge reindex hook completes on mercury-infra + any other consumer that has installed (from operator-triggered wave-2 installs) within the 60s budget from PR3.

## SCOPE

- NEW: src/service_knowledge/eval/
  - corpus/*.json — labeled cases
  - harness.py — runs the corpus, computes metrics
  - metrics.py — metric definitions + aggregation
  - reports/  — output artifacts
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/index/query.py — telemetry emission on every query (PR3 declared the table; this PR populates it)

- NEW: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/.github/workflows/eval-weekly.yml — cron running eval harness, publishing report as artifact + sticky-commenting summary on a tracking issue

## NON_GOALS

- No cross-repo aggregation switch (metrics might trigger it — follow-up)

title: substrate §4.3: add 5th coordinator role (incident handler) + runtime.* failure kinds + closed:failed-as-verdict invariant
description:
Folds three coupled findings from the premortem cross-doc audit (~/dev/xtrm/docs/premortem-substrate/) into substrate_design_it.md.

# Problem

§4.3 enumerates 4 coordinator roles: (1) entry gate, (2) borderline judge, (3) cross-chain hygiene via pulse, (4) close-time judge with memory distillation. None of them is the *runtime incident handler*. The close-time fallback covers "coordinator cant write coordinator.release after N respawns → §5.10 failure-distillation terminal fallback" — but that is the LLM-coordinator failing to *close* cleanly. It does not cover mid-run mechanical failures:

- executor died mid-step (no agent_end within budget)
- gate dispatched but no verdict within T
- worktree diverged (base moved, branch cant FF)
- evidence ref broken (referenced file/event missing)
- pulse delivery failed after N attempts (cross-chain hygiene)
- budget exhausted mid-step
- recursion cap on coordinator-restitch loops

Today these fall through to the orchestrator. The orchestrator owns *vision* (§4.3 due giudici, scope distinti), not intra-chain mechanics — wrong authority for runtime triage. Chain ends up closed:failed by runtime fallthrough rather than by an explicit judge verdict.

# Proposal

## 1. Add coordinator role #5 in §4.3 (incident handler durante esecuzione)

> Il reducer è anche detector di failure meccanici. Su categorie deterministiche tenta recovery automatica (idempotency-keyed retry per transient errors, requeue per pulse dropped, respawn-via-journal §5.9 per context-window). Quando il recovery deterministico esaurisce il retry_budget o la failure è judgment-shaped (es. "executor morto dopo write parziale al worktree"), emette `chain.incident{kind, detected_at, mechanical_recovery_attempts, evidence_refs}`. Il coordinator sottoscrive `chain.incident.*` e decide entro autonomy: `retry_with_modifier`, `restitch_from_evidence:<ref>`, `escalate`, oppure `verdict: failed` con distillazione esplicita.

## 2. Add runtime.* failure kinds to channels §7 vocabulary

- runtime.participant_died
- runtime.gate_unresponsive
- runtime.worktree_diverged
- runtime.evidence_ref_broken
- runtime.pulse_delivery_failed
- runtime.budget_exhausted_mid_step
- runtime.recursion_cap

(channels §7 already defines runtime.message_rejected and runtime.delivery_failed — extends the same family.)

## 3. Add invariant to §3.1 (due layer di giudizio sempre presenti)

> Un chain non fallisce mai per runtime fallthrough. Raggiunge `closed:done` via `coordinator.release` o `closed:failed` via verdict esplicito del coordinator. Lunico modo in cui un chain può morire SENZA verdict del coordinator è substrate-level unavailability (state.db unwritable, daemon crash) — failure class separata, owned dal substrate kernel, propagata come `substrate.unavailable` allorchestrator.

## 4. Critical constraint: reducer stays pure (channels §11)

Detection happens IN the reducer (mechanical state observation). The wake-coordinator intent is emitted by the after-hook with an idempotency key — exactly the pattern §11 already enforces for "reducer pure, side effects in after-hook". This is why detection must NOT call LLM/wake directly; it emits a chain.incident event and the after-hook is what actually wakes the coordinator subscriber.

## 5. Cost containment

- Reducer attempts deterministic mechanical recovery FIRST (idempotent retry, requeue) — most transient failures get fixed without waking the coordinator
- Coordinator only wakes when recovery_attempts >= threshold OR failure class is judgment-shaped
- Coordinator subscribes to chain.incident.* (selective subscription per channels §8 audience model) — does not read runtime.* observability stream
- Existing autonomy budget bounds restitch loops (§5.10 hard_cap pattern)

# Why

Premortem reason §6 (chain coordinator over-specified) PARTIAL verdict was driven by missing crisp policy for runtime incident handling. The audit also flagged §4.3 close-time fallback as the only documented failure path — confirming the runtime gap. User instinct ("chain shall not entirely fail by design — but I might be wrong") maps to the weaker, defensible form: chain failure should be a *judge decision*, never a *runtime outcome*. Kernel-level disasters still terminate, but at a different layer.

# Scope

- docs/substrate/substrate_design_it.md §3.1 (invariant), §4.3 (5th role)
- docs/channels/channels_plain_it.md §7 (runtime.* kinds vocabulary)
- docs/premortem-substrate/audit-result.md (note R6 revised: PARTIAL → ADDRESSED once 5th role + invariant are folded in)

# Non-goals

- Implementing the runtime detector in specialists code (substrate is design-only until the substrate-bridge epic ships)
- Defining the exact wire format of chain.incident (channels §11 idempotency key shape will dictate)
- Resurrection / "all participants died" recovery — out of scope; substrate.unavailable handles that
- sp merge / sp epic merge rework (separate epic per CLAUDE.md gotcha)

# Validation

- Each runtime.* kind listed in §4.3 maps to an existing failure mode the orchestrator handles today
- §3.1 invariant survives a "what if state.db dies" probe (answer: substrate.unavailable, different class)
- Reducer purity (channels §11) is preserved — detection IN reducer, wake intent in after-hook with idempotency key
- Cost-bounding reasoning in #5 above remains valid given the channels §8 audience model

# Output

Three doc patches landed in substrate_design_it.md + channels_plain_it.md + a short note in audit-result.md updating R6.

# Discovered from

Premortem cross-doc audit ~/dev/xtrm/docs/premortem-substrate/ (synthesis.md + audit-result.md, 2026-06-13 session).

Plus ripple: chain_templates.md §2.9 + §3 incident-policy table for all 15 templates; forensic-event-contract.md §6 new chain.incident.* family with cardinality/redaction. All cross-references resolve.

title: Enable SSH commit signing + required_signatures on xtrm main
description:
## PROBLEM

Branch protection on xtrm-dev/xtrm main is now tight (1 approval, enforce_admins true, last_push_approval true, no force push / deletions, conversation resolution required, linear history), BUT `required_signatures` was left disabled to avoid locking the owner out — there is no local signing key configured in git, no `~/.gnupg/`, and the recent commits on main are unverified.

## SUCCESS

`required_signatures` is enabled on main protection, the local git is configured to sign by default with the existing `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, and a verification push lands a commit that GitHub shows as "Verified".

## SCOPE

- Local git config (user.signingkey, gpg.format=ssh, commit.gpgsign=true, gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile).
- GitHub account: register `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` as a signing key (separate from auth-key registration).
- Re-enable `required_signatures` on `repos/xtrm-dev/xtrm/branches/main/protection/required_signatures`.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Use SSH signing with the existing ed25519 key — no GPG bootstrap required.
- Operator must run the local config commands themselves; do not assume an agent can install signing without consent.

## VALIDATION

Exact steps to run, in order:

```bash
# 1. Tell git to sign with SSH using the existing ed25519 key
git config --global gpg.format ssh
git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
git config --global commit.gpgsign true
git config --global tag.gpgsign true

# 2. (Optional) Build an allowed-signers file so `git log --show-signature`
#    can verify locally
mkdir -p ~/.config/git
printf '%s %s\n' "$(git config user.email)" "$(cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub)" \
  > ~/.config/git/allowed_signers
git config --global gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile ~/.config/git/allowed_signers

# 3. Register the SSH key as a SIGNING key on GitHub (separate from auth key)
gh ssh-key add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --type signing --title "$(hostname) signing"

# 4. Re-enable required_signatures on main
gh api -X POST repos/xtrm-dev/xtrm/branches/main/protection/required_signatures \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json"

# 5. Verify: make a trivial commit on a branch, push, and check it lands as Verified
gh api repos/xtrm-dev/xtrm/commits/main --jq '.commit.verification'
```

## NON_GOALS

- GPG/PGP setup (not needed when SSH signing works).
- Configuring other repos in the org (do those one at a time, this bead is xtrm only).
- Backfilling signatures on existing unsigned commits — pre-protection history is exempt.

## OUTPUT

- Final `required_signatures.enabled = true` on main protection.
- One signed test commit visible as Verified in GitHub UI.

## REFERENCES

- GitHub docs on SSH commit signing: https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification#ssh-commit-signature-verification
- Current branch protection: 1 approval, enforce_admins, last_push_approval, linear history, no force push, no deletions, conversation resolution required.
- Branch protection was tightened in this session (2026-06-10) — every other guard is on; only signing is deferred until the operator runs the steps above.

SCRUTINY: low

title: Verify mcpq wiring in mercury-infra: scripted, sidecars-up-gated smoke
description:
## PROBLEM

xtrm-2m3 epic Phase D shipped a `.mcpq.json` in `~/projects/mercury/infra` and PR mercuryintelligence/infra#76 to merge it. End-to-end was verified once from the orchestrator on 2026-06-10 against the live sidecars (`infra-prometheus-mcp` + `infra-grafana-mcp`). That single verification covers happy paths. To consider the mercury-infra integration durable, the infra repo should carry its OWN scripted verification (gated on sidecars-up) so anyone bootstrapping the repo can prove the wiring works without a one-off interactive session.

## SUCCESS

A scripted verification lives in `~/projects/mercury/infra/scripts/` (or `tests/`) that:
1. Detects whether both sidecars are up via `docker ps --filter`.
2. If down: prints clear instructions to start them (or skips).
3. If up: runs the canonical smokes against `.mcpq.json` and asserts the expected shapes:
   - `mcpq servers` lists exactly `grafana` and `prometheus`.
   - `mcpq prometheus list-tools` returns exactly 6 `mercury_*`-prefixed tools.
   - `mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job="prometheus"}'` returns a vector with at least one sample value (`"1"` or numeric 1).
   - `mcpq grafana list-tools` returns ≥40 tools.
   - `mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards` shows the input schema with `query`/`limit`/`page`.
4. Exit 0 on success, non-zero with a clear diagnostic on failure.
5. Wired into whatever infra-side check harness already exists (`scripts/`, `Makefile`, CI workflow) — match the project's existing patterns rather than introducing a new one.
6. Documents the script in mercury-infra's README or a focused doc under `docs/`.

## SCOPE

- Mercury-infra repo only (`~/projects/mercury/infra`).
- New file(s) under `scripts/` or `tests/` per repo convention.
- Optional doc under `docs/` or `README.md` snippet.
- DO NOT touch the xtrm repo or `packages/mcpq`.

## NON_GOALS

- New unit coverage of `mcpq` internals (that's already in xtrm/packages/mcpq/tests).
- Live-call assertions on tool outputs beyond basic shape (no "prometheus must have N targets") — drift would be expected and false-positives hurt.
- Auth header tests (sidecars use static env-var creds; no rotation to verify).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Use whatever language matches infra repo conventions (bash + jq, python3, etc.).
- Script must be runnable standalone without setting up a Python venv that doesn't already exist in the operator's path — install instructions belong in docs, not in the script.
- Sidecar-up detection MUST gracefully skip rather than fail when sidecars are down (this script should be idempotent in any environment state).
- Telemetry one-liner on stderr from `mcpq` MUST be ignored or asserted as JSON — don't let it leak into stdout parsing.
- This is a SEPARATE issue from PR #76 — that PR just lands the `.mcpq.json`; this bead is the verification harness that exercises it.

## VALIDATION

- Run the script locally with sidecars up — exits 0, prints expected counts.
- Run with one sidecar down — prints skip message, exits 0 (or whatever the repo convention is for skipped checks).
- CI workflow (if applicable) picks up the script and runs it.
- README/docs reference the script and what it asserts.

## OUTPUT

- New verification script(s) and any wiring (Makefile target, CI job, etc.).
- Doc snippet showing how to run it.
- Confirmation that PR #76 is merged before this can be tested end-to-end (or that the script reads `.mcpq.json` from a known path either way).

## REFERENCES

- xtrm-2m3 epic (closed 2026-06-10) — full mcpq CLI shipped at xtrm/packages/mcpq/
- xtrm-2m3.7 (closed) — initial mercury-infra wiring + one-off verification
- PR: https://github.com/mercuryintelligence/infra/pull/76 (`.mcpq.json` for the two sidecars)
- xtrm Phase D smoke test pattern: packages/mcpq/tests/test_smoke.py (already gates on `docker ps`; mercury-infra script can mirror the same approach)
- xtrm install path expected on host: `pip install -e <xtrm-repo>/packages/mcpq` (or the future PyPI release)

SCRUTINY: medium
close_reason: Shipped scripts/verify_mcpq.py + 'make verify-mcpq' target + doc section in docs/telemetry/mcp-query-surfaces.md. Five live-shape assertions (servers, prom count + mercury_ prefix, prom execute_query == 1, grafana count >= 40, grafana describe search_dashboards has limit/page/query). Sidecars-up gate: skips with clear remediation when missing; exits 0 in both ok and skip paths. --json mode for machine consumers. Verified both paths locally (ok with all sidecars up, skip when one stopped). PR scope: piggybacks on PR #76 (mcpq integration) since it's the same logical unit.

description:

title: P1.3 — via-mode dispatch: host + docker:<container>
description:
## PROBLEM
The sidecars in mercury-infra are on a Docker network with no host port. Direct urllib from the host fails (DNS not resolvable). Need an indirection layer that runs the HTTP call from inside a Docker container which IS on the network.

## SUCCESS
A `via_call(via_spec, request)` function that dispatches:
- `via: host` → direct urllib call (transparent passthrough)
- `via: docker:<container>` → `docker exec -i <container> curl ...` with proper body piping + header forwarding + response capture
The protocol layer (P1.2) uses this for every HTTP exchange.

## SCOPE
- `mcpq/via.py` (or in single-file): `via_call(spec: str, method: str, url: str, headers: dict, body: bytes) -> (status: int, response_headers: dict, response_body: bytes)`
- Tested against the actual mercury-infra `infra-prometheus-mcp` container as the curl host

## NON_GOALS
- via modes beyond host + docker (no ssh, no docker-net spawn, no kubectl) — these are roadmap, not v1
- Latency optimization (each docker exec spawns a process; fine for now)

## CONSTRAINTS
- Target container for `docker:<container>` must have curl; document this in error message if missing
- Docker exec must use `-i` (interactive) to pipe request body via stdin
- Response headers parsed from `curl -i` output (status + headers + body separated by blank line)
- Failure modes surface clearly: "container not running", "curl not in container", "container not on network"

## VALIDATION
- [ ] `via_call("host", ...)` works against any reachable HTTP URL
- [ ] `via_call("docker:infra-prometheus-mcp", ...)` works against http://infra-grafana-mcp:8090/mcp from the host
- [ ] Error: nonexistent container → clear error message
- [ ] Error: container exists but no curl → clear error message
- [ ] Telemetry includes via mode + container name in jsonl

## OUTPUT
A via dispatch module. P1.2 protocol layer rewires to use it. P2.x subcommands inherit transparently.

title: P1.2 — MCP protocol client + .mcpq.json discovery
description:
## PROBLEM
Core protocol mechanics. Must handshake with any MCP server (initialize → initialized notification → tools/list / tools/call), maintain session-id, parse SSE-framed responses, and read per-project server registry from .mcpq.json discovered by walking up cwd.

## SUCCESS
A `MCPClient` class (or equivalent module-level fns) handles the full handshake → call cycle against a URL. A `find_config()` helper walks up from cwd, returns the parsed .mcpq.json content with validation. Both work standalone (unit-testable without a live server).

## SCOPE
- `mcpq/protocol.py` (or in single-file): `init_session(url) -> (session_id, server_info)`, `list_tools(url, sid)`, `call_tool(url, sid, name, args)`, `parse_sse(text)`
- `mcpq/config.py`: `find_config() -> Path | None`, `load_config(path) -> ConfigSchema`, schema validation (servers dict, name keys, url + via required)
- `.mcpq.json` schema documented at top of config.py and in README

## NON_GOALS
- via-mode dispatch (P1.3 handles it; this module just exposes URL-direct calls)
- Subcommand UX (P2.x); this layer is pure protocol + config

## CONSTRAINTS
- Case-insensitive header lookup for `Mcp-Session-Id` (servers differ in casing)
- SSE parser must handle both `event: message\ndata: {json}` (Prom MCP via FastMCP) and plain JSON (Grafana MCP)
- All HTTP calls use urllib (no third-party)
- Telemetry hook point: emit `{ts, server, op, duration_ms, outcome}` to stderr at module-call boundaries

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Unit test: `parse_sse` with both SSE and plain-JSON inputs returns dict
- [ ] Unit test: `find_config` walks up to root, returns None gracefully if missing
- [ ] Unit test: config schema rejects missing `via`, missing `url`, unknown extra keys
- [ ] Manual: against live infra-prometheus-mcp on host (after host port bound or via direct curl), full handshake completes
- [ ] Telemetry jsonl visible on stderr for each protocol op

## OUTPUT
A protocol module + config module, unit-tested. P1.3 wraps both with via-mode dispatch.

title: mcpq — CLI + skill for querying Docker-sidecar MCP servers without .mcp.json bloat
description:
## PROBLEM

xtrm projects increasingly run OSS MCP servers (Grafana MCP, Prometheus MCP, future Loki/Tempo MCPs) as Docker sidecars on internal networks for substrate/specialist-agent use. Two problems with the obvious `.mcp.json` wiring path: (a) the sidecars are internal-only by design (no host port — defense in depth), so the host's Claude Code can't reach them at all; (b) even when host-reachable, loading 49+ tool schemas per session burns ~18k tokens of always-loaded context regardless of whether observability work happens that session. No existing CLI bridges this — `mcp-client`-style tools assume host-reachable URLs and stdio transport.

## SUCCESS

A `mcpq` CLI is installable from `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/` and available from any xtrm project. Subcommands: `mcpq servers`, `mcpq <name> list-tools`, `mcpq <name> describe <tool>`, `mcpq <name> call <tool> --arg key=val`. Tool catalog discovered live every call (no hard-coded schemas — image bumps don't break docs). A skill (`using-mcpq`) auto-loads when needed, teaches discovery, stays under ~150 lines regardless of server tool count. In mercury-infra, the two existing sidecars (`infra-grafana-mcp` 49 tools, `infra-prometheus-mcp` 6 tools) are reachable via `via: docker:<container>` indirection — no host port exposure.

## SCOPE

- New package: `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/` — first package in xtrm/packages/, establishes convention
- Per-project config: `<repo>/.mcpq.json` (CLI walks up cwd; mirrors `.mcp.json` discovery)
- Skill: `~/dev/xtrm/packages/mcpq/skills/using-mcpq/SKILL.md`
- Integration: `mercury-infra/.mcpq.json` referencing the existing two sidecars
- No changes to MCP sidecar deployment configs themselves

## NON_GOALS

- stdio transport (HTTP + streamable-http only in v1)
- Auth flows beyond static env-var injection at server-deploy time
- Multi-server batch calls or result caching
- Replacing `.mcp.json` for low-tool-count MCPs that benefit from native wiring
- A writable MCP variant (read-only is the design)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Python 3.10+ stdlib only (no third-party deps on the call path — trivial install)
- Per-server `via` field required; minimum two modes: `host` (direct urllib) and `docker:<container>` (exec into running Docker-network container; reuses its `curl`)
- SSE response framing must be parsed: handles both `event: message\ndata: {...}` and plain JSON shapes (different MCP servers use different framings)
- Session-id header matched case-insensitively (`Mcp-Session-Id` and `mcp-session-id` both seen)
- Tool catalog NEVER hard-coded — every list-tools/describe hits the server live
- Skill body capped ~150 lines; does NOT enumerate tools
- Telemetry: every invocation logs `{timestamp, server, subcommand, tool, duration_ms, outcome}` to stderr as one-line JSON; no payloads, no secrets

## VALIDATION

- [ ] \`mcpq prometheus call mercury_execute_query --arg query='up{job=\"prometheus\"}'\` returns vector with value=1 against running mercury-infra sidecars
- [ ] \`mcpq grafana call search_dashboards\` returns live dashboard list (≥10 entries)
- [ ] \`mcpq grafana describe search_dashboards\` prints input schema (typed args, required, defaults)
- [ ] \`mcpq grafana list-tools\` returns ≥40 tools (live count from sidecar at v0.15.2)
- [ ] \`mcpq prometheus list-tools\` returns exactly 6 tools (prom-mcp v1.6.1 with TOOL_PREFIX=mercury)
- [ ] Skill \`using-mcpq\` triggers on observability/MCP-query prompts; does not pre-load otherwise
- [ ] Smoke test gated on sidecars-up exists in tests/ and passes locally
- [ ] README.md documents install + per-project setup + the `via` semantics
- [ ] Telemetry jsonl observed on stderr for each invocation (greppable via \`mcpq ... 2>&1 | jq\`)

## OUTPUT

On epic close: link to merged PR(s), summary of CLI surface, verified mercury-infra invocations, cross-project portability notes (which other xtrm projects could adopt `.mcpq.json` now), and any drift findings discovered against the upstream sidecar images during test.

## REFERENCES

- mercury-infra session 2026-06-10 (infra-6if close-out) — context that motivated this epic
- mercury-infra: \`docs/telemetry/mcp-query-surfaces.md\`, \`docs/telemetry/devops-query-surface-eval.md\`
- mercury-infra service skills: \`.xtrm/skills/user/packs/infra/service-skills/services/{grafana,prometheus}-mcp/SKILL.md\`
- xtrm: \`docs/devops/mcp-sidecars-pattern.md\`
- Upstream: github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana, github.com/pab1it0/prometheus-mcp-server
- MCP spec: github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification
close_reason:
Epic complete. mcpq Python CLI shipped at xtrm/packages/mcpq/ across 4 phases:

Phase A (xtrm-2m3.10, merge 2ac44b4): scaffold + protocol client + via-mode dispatch + .mcpq.json discovery. 12 files. Stdlib-only call path. Security hardening (F-1 SSRF allowlist, F-2 CRLF guard, F-3 walk-up bound, F-4 container regex). Reviewer PASS 98/100.

Phase B (xtrm-2m3.17, merge 3615e5c): list-tools, describe, call subcommands with typed args (str/int/float/bool/json). Live-verified.

Phase C (xtrm-2m3.22, merge 55eda90): README (175 lines) + using-mcpq skill (125 lines, auto-trigger description).

Phase D (xtrm-2m3.9, merge 618f737): 84/84 tests pass (77 unit + 7 smoke gated on docker ps). cli.py mcpq servers bug fix.

mercury-infra integration (xtrm-2m3.7): .mcpq.json + PR mercuryintelligence/infra#76 (branch protection blocks direct merge — user merges when ready).

All 9 child beads closed. Live end-to-end verified against mercury_platform sidecars: prometheus 6 mercury_* tools, grafana 49 tools, mercury_execute_query 'up' returns vector value=1.

description:

No TUI changes; no stdout pollution.

title: Info-level polish backlog (F14-F17)
description:
# PROBLEM

Four info-level observations from the review, no correctness impact, deferred by design. (F14) writeClipboard (src/clipboard.mjs:12) has no OSC 52 payload-size guard; near-1600-token rewrites can exceed terminal clipboard caps (4-16KB) and silently no-op with exit 0. (F15) Interactive SIGINT (cli.mjs readline handler) does not abort an in-flight refinement call; the initial rewrite at app.mjs:115 is not abortable; exit 130 only happens after the in-flight call returns. (F16) --context has no escape for literal @-prefixed text (src/app.mjs:197 always treats @x as a file path). (F17) writeClipboard's return value ("OSC 52"/"tmux OSC 52") is never consumed (src/app.mjs:145).

# SUCCESS

Each item is either implemented with a test or closed as wont-fix with a recorded reason on this bead. Suggested scope per item: F14 a size warning (>~8KB base64) on stderr before sending; F15 wiring Ctrl-C into the completion AbortSignal once readline is active and documenting the initial-call behavior; F16 a documented escape (e.g. leading backslash) or README note; F17 removing the return value or consuming it in a diagnostic.

# SCOPE

src/clipboard.mjs, src/app.mjs (runInteractive/completeRewrite signal wiring :235-328,350-381; readContext :195-206; clipboardOptions :343-348), src/cli.mjs (openInteractive :16-46), README.md, tests as needed.

# NON_GOALS

- None of these block the epic; if a fix is rejected, the reason is recorded here and the item stays closed as wont-fix.

# CONSTRAINTS

- F15 must not change the documented exit-code contract (Ctrl-C during a read stays 130).
- F14 must not turn a copy failure into a different exit code than the documented 1 for clipboard failure.
- No new dependencies.

# VALIDATION

- [ ] Each adopted item has a test; each rejected item has a wont-fix note on this bead.
- [ ] Full suite green.
- [ ] README documents any behavior change (clipboard size caveat, SIGINT abort, @ escape).

# OUTPUT

Per-item decision (implemented with evidence, or wont-fix with reason), changed files, test evidence.
close_reason: F14-F17 fixed (no wont-fix): OSC 52 >8KB base64 stderr warning (copy proceeds, exit codes unchanged); interactive Ctrl-C aborts in-flight refinement via AbortController -> 130 without 'timed out'; '@@' escape yields literal @ without file read (documented); writeClipboard return removed, consumers cleaned. README updated. 66 tests green.

In a one-shot prompt rewriter, interactive clarification belongs to the CLI boundary only. The model rewrite contract must not tell the model to ask the user; missing facts should become inspection steps, assumptions to verify, or open questions inside the rewritten prompt. Validate and retry one-line clarification-only model outputs because sentinel structure alone does not prove semantic correctness.

Standalone ModelRuntime CLIs should read Pi SettingsManager defaultProvider/defaultModel before falling back to ModelRuntime.getAvailable()[0]. Catalog order can select a weak but authenticated model (observed nvidia/google/gemma-3-4b-it) that fails strict response envelopes; the configured Pi default produced a valid xtprompt rewrite.

A prompt-refinement CLI can provide chain-like interaction without AgentSession by retaining only current and previous valid prompts. Each free-text turn sends current prompt plus the latest refinement instruction through completeSimple; failed rewrites preserve state. Commands remain local state transitions, and :accept is the only clipboard/exit transition.

For a remote-friendly CLI clipboard option, keep the normal result on stdout and send Base64 OSC 52 control bytes through a separate TTY control stream (stderr in xtprompt). Wrap OSC 52 in tmux passthrough when TMUX is set. A successful write only proves dispatch, not that the terminal accepted the clipboard update because OSC 52 has no acknowledgment.
